rooms.title: Farstone QBN Design
rooms.description: Design note testing whether Farstone's quality-based-narrative turn needs a new substrate, against the two real Farstone artifacts (the pyfars governance polity and the built tab/FizzOS MUD): verdict, core loop, content pipeline, qualities, prose-at-volume risk, staircase placement, and the cast.
rooms.body:
# Farstone QBN Design

Prompted by the owner, 2026-08-19: "Which makes me wonder if that's not what Farstone shouldn't
turn into" — Farstone as a quality-based narrative (QBN) game in the register of *Sunless Sea* and
*Kingdom of Loathing*: text-forward, character state as named qualities, content as storylets
gated on and modifying qualities.

There are two real Farstone artifacts, not one. Naming them precisely, because the whole design
turns on the difference:

- **The pyfars polity** — an in-fiction municipality (Mayor Aliyah Reyes, Harbormaster Takeshi
  Aoki, city hall, a permit backlog) authored as markdown-plus-frontmatter governance records that
  a Python engine (`pyfars`) dispatches work against. Lives at
  `lib/legacy/2026-08-17-vps-561-group/_archive/code/pyfars/examples/farstone/`.
- **`@561-group/farstone`** — a *built* MUD: JavaScript game content riding the `tab` EAVT
  world-engine and the FizzOS MUD driver, servable today over HTTP/SSE and playable in a browser.
  Lives at `lib/legacy/2026-08-17-vps-561-group/_archive/from-content-source/apps/games/farstone/`.
  Its own README states the mechanic the owner is pointing at directly: *"Building Permit #23 ages
  under its own clock past its decision window and goes ⊤ on its own; nobody coded 'permits go
  bad,' the bilattice fold produced it."*

## Thesis verdict

**Partly true, and the part that's false matters more than the part that's true.** The MUD's
fold-produced ⊤-situations really are storylet-shaped — a quality settling to a value nobody
scripted, surfaced as content, is the actual mechanism, not a metaphor for it, and it is already
running in committed code (§1 below, with the receipts). But the pyfars records and the MUD world
are **not** two serializations of one town. They are two independently-implemented artifacts, in
two different languages, on two different engines, that share a common ancestor and were
deliberately **re-ported "for vibe not for specifics"** — the MUD's own `farstone/README.md` says
so in those words — which is provably true at the level of a single NPC's biography (§1) and
provably *not* true at the level of engine mechanics, permit numbering, or named cast (§1). A QBN
Farstone cannot compile both into one world; it has to pick a spine. The recommended spine, and
why, is in §6.

## 1. Are the fold-situations and the records actually storylets? (with receipts)

### 1a. The MUD: a quality settling to ⊤ nobody scripted

The seed-island world (`farstone/`, built by `build-farstone.mjs`) carries Building Permit #23 as
five EAVT rows, quoted verbatim from `farstone/permit-23.jsonl`:

```
{"e":"permit-23","a":"kind","v":"item","t":"seed:000106"}
{"e":"permit-23","a":"naming","v":"Building Permit #23","t":"seed:000107"}
{"e":"permit-23","a":"describing","v":"One of fourteen applications before Building & Safety; the charter requires a decision inside thirty days.","t":"seed:000108"}
{"e":"permit-23","a":"located-in","v":"downtown-farston","t":"seed:000109"}
{"e":"permit-23","a":"within-window","v":"building-permit","t":"seed:000110"}
{"e":"within-window","a":"has-converse","v":"overdue","t":"seed:000111"}
```

The last row is the whole mechanism: `within-window` is declared to have the converse
`overdue`. Nothing else is authored. The `farstone/README.md` explains what happens next: run the
world forward and *"Permit #23 ages; past tick 30 the world files `overdue`, and against its
standing `within-window` assertion the cell settles to ⊤."* That is a quality (`permit-23`'s
window-state) changing value as a pure function of elapsed world-time, with no storylet author
writing an `if (daysSincefiled > 30)` branch anywhere — the branch is a property of the bilattice
join (`⊤` = both `within-window` and its converse `overdue` are witnessed at once), triggered by
one `declareConverse` binding made once. This is genuinely the mechanism a QBN engine needs: **a
quality is a settled EAVT cell, and a storylet is a situation the fold makes visible.** The fog-bell
/ harbormaster pattern in the same world is the same shape at smaller grain — `takeshi-aoki.jsonl`
carries `{"a":"intends","v":{"when":{"predicate":"ringing","object":"for-fog"},"do":{"predicate":"tending","object":"the-fog-bell"}}}` — an NPC reflex keyed off a perceived quality-change, which is
exactly a KoL "an NPC does X when quality Y flips" hook, authored as one data row.

### 1b. pyfars: the *same convention*, authored a different way

pyfars encodes the identical "permit ages past a 30-day window into a violation" convention, but as
hand-written conditional logic rather than an emergent fold. From
`governance/duties/decide-permit-within-30-days.md`:

> *"An application whose `received-at` is more than 30 calendar days old without a decision record
> produces `(application, charter-bound-c5, jurisdictional-boundaries-violated) = T` and
> `(building-safety-director, charter-binding-violated, true) = T`."*

And a live instance of it, `work/tasks/municipal/decide-permit-application-2026-117.md`, filed
2026-06-22, **"27 of 30 days elapsed"** at time of authoring, with an explicit consequence: *"If a
decision is not filed by 2026-07-22, the substrate fires `(building-safety-director,
charter-binding-violated, true) = T`, the eligibility-by-charter-binding rule disqualifies the
office from new permits until any held application gets a decision."* pyfars's own closure-rule
records (`objects/tide-derivation.md`, `objects/opening-hours-derivation.md`) show it, too, runs on
a `reads` → `writes` cells-in/cells-out shape with a `fires-during: settling` cadence — structurally
the same *kind* of thing tab's closure engine does. So both engines are genuinely
closure-over-cells systems. The difference is where the trigger condition lives: tab's `T` above is
a **free consequence of the algebra** (declare one converse, get "ages into contradiction" for any
predicate with that shape, forever); pyfars's `T` is a **per-record authored consequent** (someone
had to write "more than 30 calendar days... produces `T`" into this specific duty file, and it only
fires for permits, because nobody wrote the analogous rule for anything else). Both are
storylet-shaped. Only one is free.

### 1c. The relationship between the two artifacts: shared lineage, not shared substrate

Proof of shared ancestry, quoted rather than inferred. The MUD's `farstone/` seed island names
eleven places by exact slug — `mt-farstone`, `the-ridge`, `downtown-farston`, `harbor-district`,
`farston-harbor`, `south-point-light`, `farr-river`, `farr-valley`, `north-shore`, `the-marsh`,
`marsh-end` (`farstone.jsonl`) — against pyfars's `governance/places/_index.md`, which names the
identical set: `farstone-island`, `mt-farstone`, `town-of-farston`, `downtown-farston`,
`harbor-district`, `marsh-end`, `the-ridge`, `farr-valley`, `north-shore`, `the-marsh`, `farr-river`,
`farston-harbor`, `south-point-light`. Eleven of eleven MUD place-slugs are pyfars place-slugs. And
at the level of a single character, the match is verbatim. The MUD's `takeshi-aoki.jsonl`:

> *"Thirty years on the water; lives aboard his sloop in the warm half of the year, a rented flat
> above the harbor café in winter."*

pyfars's `governance/agents/harbormaster-takeshi.md`:

> *"...thirty-plus-year career in commercial fishing before taking the office in 2023. Lives on a
> sailboat moored at the harbor in the warm half of the year, in a rented flat above
> [`harbor-cafe`]... in winter."*

That is not coincidence; the MUD's own README says exactly this happened: *"Farstone is ported, for
vibe not for specifics, from the prior Farstone in the tab archive... and from the PyFARS governance
Farstone under the predication-categories bucket."* But "for vibe not for specifics" is provably
true too: **Aliyah Reyes — pyfars's Mayor of Farston — does not appear anywhere in the MUD's named
cast.** The MUD's permit is `permit-23`, a *building* permit; the designed `farstone-tale/` world
(a third, separate MUD content-pack — see below) independently reinvents *"App. 23"* as **a
different permit** — `the-dredging-permit`, contested between two fishers, not Building & Safety.
pyfars's live permit instance is numbered `2026-117`, not 23, and concerns a rear-deck addition, not
a building generally. Three different "aging permit → contradiction" storylet-instances across the
corpus, none sharing an ID, all converging on the same 30-day-window convention independently. That
convergence — not a shared file — is the actual continuity between the artifacts.

**One correction to the framing this task opened with:** the brief names Aliyah Reyes as "clerk."
The current pyfars agent record (`governance/agents/aliyah-reyes.md`) makes her **Mayor of
Farston**, not the clerk — records-clerk duties belong to a separate office
(`governance/offices/records-clerk.md`, partly automated by `records-clerk-bot`). An earlier corpus
document, the 2026-05-09 friction report cited in §3, does call her *"an in-fiction Farston staffer
(the city clerk)"* — so the corpus's own internal continuity drifted between authoring passes. That
drift is itself a small, honest data point for §4: a hand-authored governance record has no engine
enforcing that "Aliyah Reyes is the clerk" and "Aliyah Reyes is the Mayor" can't both be true at
once across two files; an EAVT trace would hold that as a legible ⊤, not a silent inconsistency
found by a human three months later.

**Also, on the MUD side, "the world" is not singular.** `@561-group/farstone` ships *four* content
packs sharing one engine (`farstone/`, `farstone-harbor/`, `farstone-tale/`, `farstone-wild/`, all
enumerated in the top-level `games/farstone/README.md`), and only one of them —
`farstone-harbor/`, "quarrel on the quay" — is what `bin/farstone.mjs` actually serves today. It is
the dense, hand-authored ~30-room tutorial-plus-waterfront world, not the seed island that carries
Permit #23. So even inside the single MUD artifact, "the town" already means at least two different
things depending which content pack is loaded.

## 2. The core loop

**A KoL-style daily action budget is a good genre fit, but it is not the house's daily-seed pattern,
and treating them as the same thing would be a mistake.** The house convention, attested in
`gaming-enterprises-vision.md`'s staircase table (*"ruinfold-daily — the shared daily ritual, one
seed, everyone, satoshi settlement"*) and in `the-suite-and-the-studio.md`'s Today-page proposal
(*"today's ruinfold dungeon, today's crucible tangle... same seeds for everyone"*), is about
**content determinism**: one seed produces one board/situation-set that every player sees
identically, replay-verifiable. KoL's adventures/turns mechanic is about **per-player pacing**: a
personal, refilling resource spent across storylets, independent of what anyone else has. These are
orthogonal axes, and Farstone's engine already gives each one a natural home without conflating
them:

- **Daily seed → which situations are live.** Tide phase, weather, which permits are within-window
  vs. aging toward ⊤, which NPC routines are active (`farstone-harbor`'s `README.md`: *"Yorrick
  works his shop by day and drinks at the inn by night... where you find someone depends on the
  hour"*) — all of this is already clock-derived state in both artifacts (tab's `ticking`, pyfars's
  `world-clock` + cadence stack). A house daily seed should govern *today's* tide/weather/permit-
  docket, shared by every player, exactly like ruinfold's dungeon.
- **Action budget → a per-player quality, spent independently.** This is a new quality the engine
  doesn't have yet (needs/hunger/rest decay toward zero; an action budget refills toward a cap) but
  it composes cleanly on the existing substrate — it's one more functional cell (`you`'s
  `actions-remaining`), decremented by `doing`, refilled by a tick-boundary rule the same shape as
  `world-cadence-boundary-detection`.

Judged, not assumed: the genre needs scarcity to make a choice matter (Sunless Sea's fuel/supplies,
KoL's adventures are the same lever), and the engine already has the primitives (functional cells,
tick-gated writes) to build it cheaply. The mistake would be trying to make the *daily seed itself*
the action-budget mechanism — they should be two separate qualities, one shared, one personal.

**Browser vs. terminal — this is already decided, not a live question.** `bin/farstone.mjs`'s own
usage note reads *"Open `http://localhost:18793` in a browser to play"* — the MUD already defaults
to a browser-first HTTP/SSE transport. `wheatstone` is documented as *"the client half of the
561-group MUD stack"* — a terminal client, useful for the cast (agent players connecting the way a
person would telnet in) and for anyone who wants a MUD-native feel, but not the primary surface.
This matches the house vision verbatim (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md`: *"all browser-based, with
terminal/API interfaces welcomed wherever they fit"*) — Farstone doesn't need a decision here, it
needs its existing default kept and its web client actually built out (today it's a bare HTTP/SSE
endpoint, not a QBN-shaped reading UI).

## 3. The content pipeline — the fiction-vs-deployable discriminator becomes the game's own gate

The boundary note (`2026-05-09-fictional-service-specs-vs-deployment-specs.md`) documents a real
bug: pyfars's `governance/specifications/services/pyfars-engine-farston.md` carried
`type: service-spec, status: active` while its content was pure in-fiction worldbuilding
(`host: farston-city-hall`, `authored-by: [aliyah-reyes]`) — *"The harness has no way to distinguish
'in-fiction service-spec the polity narrates as part of its world' from 'real service-spec
describing how this polity wants to be supervised.'"* The two fixes proposed there — status-based
(`status: sketch`/`fiction` skips the harness) or path-based (fictional content moves under its own
subtree) — were framed as an ops-harness problem to *avoid*.

**For a QBN Farstone, this is not a bug to route around — it is the compiler's actual selection
rule.** A game content-pipeline walking pyfars's `governance/` tree needs precisely this
discriminator, inverted: skip `type: service-spec` + `status: active` (that's infrastructure, not
content); compile everything else in `governance/{places,persons,citizens,agents,offices,duties,
skills}` plus `objects/*-derivation.md` closure-rule records into world content, because that's
already game-shaped — a `place` record IS a room, an `agent`/`citizen` record IS an NPC, a `duty`
record with a `triggering-powers` list IS a storylet's available-actions set, a
`closure-rule-record`'s `reads`/`writes` frontmatter IS already an EAVT-shaped cells-in/cells-out
contract (`tide-derivation.md`: `reads: [{subject: world-clock, predicate: current-time}, ...]`,
`writes: [{subject: farston-harbor, predicate: tide-height-m, domain: real}]`) that a tab/FizzOS
importer could translate almost mechanically into a functional predicate + closure rule.

`lantern-service`'s compiler (`src/compile.mts`, `src/frontmatter.mts`) is the closest thing the
house already has to this pipeline, and it generalizes **partially, honestly**. What ports directly:
the *shape*-rule door-extraction pattern — *"Any frontmatter key whose value is a string or array of
strings that resolves to another file in the same wing... becomes a hard door... The compiler never
hard-codes weiqi's field names"* (`DESIGN.md` §1) — is exactly the right approach for pyfars's
`contained-in`, `reports-to`, `active-holder`/`passive-party`, `serves` fields, none of which
Lantern has ever seen and none of which it needs to be told about by name. The FCA Hall-extraction
(§1, a *genuine* closed-concept lattice over a small declared attribute field set) is a legitimate
way to auto-cluster, say, every place/agent that `cites` the same charter section into a
storylet-deck. What does **not** port: Lantern has no tick, no NPC agency, no notion of a world that
changes state on its own between visits — its whole model is a static corpus a *player's memory*
decays against (the FSRS light-cone), never a *world* that decays or ages on its own. The runtime
half of a QBN Farstone — the part that actually settles `overdue`, walks NPC routines, and ticks the
tide — has to come from tab/FizzOS, not from Lantern. Lantern lends the compiler; it cannot lend the
engine.

## 4. Qualities design, grounded in what the trace actually tracks

Real cells already committed in the corpus, not invented for this note, quoted from
`farstone-harbor/world/you.jsonl` and the definitions behind them:

| kind of quality | evidence in the corpus | genre analog |
|---|---|---|
| **append-only trained stat** | `skill:fighting.melee.knife` appears as four separate witness rows ("taught ×4" per the README) before it reads as a numeric bonus | KoL's Muscle/Mysticality/Moxie — a quality that accumulates from repeated witnessed events, not a single overwrite |
| **decaying need** | `need:hunger`/`need:rest`/`need:recreation`, decremented every tick, restored by `provides`-tagged resources (`the-stew-pot`, `the-inn-beds`) | Sunless Sea's Supplies/Terror — a resource that runs down and gates what you can still do |
| **derived, not stored** | *"Your **title** is read off your governing-skill bonus — it rises as you train, no separate promotion"* (`farstone-harbor/README.md`) | Fallen London's status qualities that are pure projections of an underlying stat, never separately tracked — a real design lesson already learned here |
| **contested / ⊤-legal** | `within-window` × `overdue` on `permit-23`; pyfars's `charter-bound-c5` / `charter-binding-violated` | a quality the game is allowed to show as *both* true and false at once, and dramatize the contradiction rather than resolve it — this is the genre's "Notability"-shaped anomaly, and it's the one mechanic this substrate does better than a conventional flag-based engine |
| **relational** | `opinion-of` (Dax Pell / Mara Quill flagged `rival` of each other); pyfars's `jural-relations/` (`active-holder`/`passive-party` duty pairs) | Fallen London's "Connected: X" qualities — social state between two named entities, not a single actor's stat |
| **world-clock-derived** | pyfars's `tide-height-m`, `tide-state`, `open-now` — pure functions of `world-clock` + biome constants, recomputed each settle | Sunless Sea's weather/zee-state — ambient world quality nobody spends, but everyone reads |

The design implication: don't invent a quality taxonomy from genre conventions first and then hunt
for substrate to back it — the trace already sorts into these six families, and a QBN Farstone's
quality schema should be *read off* the union of what both artifacts already track, not designed
from scratch.

## 5. What the genre needs that the house lacks — prose at volume

Say this plainly: **agent-authored prose at Failbetter quality, at the volume the genre requires, is
not a solved problem here — it is the real risk, and the corpus itself already flags it.** The
evidence cuts both ways and both readings are honest.

The prose that exists is genuinely good at small scale. `farstone-harbor/definition.mjs` room
descriptions read like real published QBN copy — *"Granite cobbles slick with spray, bollards green
with verdigris, the fleet riding at their lines. The off-season has emptied the quay of everyone but
those who have nowhere warmer to be"* — economical, atmospheric, thematically disciplined across
~30 rooms and a dozen-plus named NPCs. That's real evidence agent-authored prose can hit a strong
register.

But volume and *branching* are the actual bar, and neither is demonstrated anywhere in this corpus.
Every world here — `farstone/`, `farstone-harbor/`, `farstone-tale/`, pyfars's governance tree — is
a single-pass authored vignette: tens of rooms, a dozen NPCs, one description each. A real QBN
storylet typically carries 500–2000 words spread across three to six branch-outcomes for a *single*
situation, times hundreds of situations (Fallen London ships on the order of a million-plus words).
Nothing in either Farstone artifact has ever been authored at that shape — variant text per
quality-gate, degrading gracefully across dozens of possible player states for the same room. The
engine's own designers already noticed the gap from the inside: `farstone-tale/README.md`'s "DSL
gaps hit while authoring" section states outright, *"No `describing` field. Areas/items/npcs get a
`naming` but no prose description... A designer authoring atmosphere has nowhere to put room/item
flavor text"* — the authoring *tool* under-serves prose today, not just the corpus. So: not solved.
The specific, nameable risk is **prose at 50–100x the volume seen here, with quality-gated
variation, sustained across many authoring sessions without voice drift** — none of which this
corpus has attempted yet, however good its small samples are.

## 6. Staircase placement + the smallest real step

Farstone does not currently appear anywhere on the staircase in `gaming-enterprises-vision.md`'s §6
table (now: weiqi/TileSlots/solitaire/flickering-delve, ruinfold-daily, Lantern/Equivo; next:
idle+gambling, energy-tiling; then: the undersea MUD, the Commons). Its natural shelf-slot is named
explicitly in `the-suite-and-the-studio.md`'s shelf table: **The Deep** — *"ruinfold daily, later the
undersea MUD and the Commons — the MUD/BBS door-games lineage."* Farstone-the-MUD is arguably ahead
of "the undersea cooperative MUD (SHRIMP ecology)" on that shelf already, in the specific sense that
its engine exists, is tested, and can be run today — but that claim needs the sober correction below
before it's a real staircase step and not a false head start.

**Sober judgment on reviving the legacy MUD vs. the active FizzOS: it is a port, not a restart, and
should be planned as one.** `bin/farstone.mjs` imports `@561-group/tab/scripts/web.mjs` and the game
content is built against the *old* fizzos lineage — the top-level MUD README lists its dependencies
as `@561-group/tab`, `@561-group/fizzos`, `@561-group/computer` (the tab/EAVT-riding generation).
The **active** fizzos, at
`services/computer-mud-services-section/apps/fizzos` (60 passed, 0 failed per its own
`content/verification-report.md`, confirmed by reading `package.json`'s `test` script and the report
together), has exactly **one** runtime dependency: `@lenticule-science/metrologic`. It does not import `tab` at
all — its own README states *"The current runtime does not import [retired implementations] and has
no build step... Retired implementations remain as read-only evidence in `lib/legacy`."* Reading
`src/world.mjs` confirms the *mechanism* survives in spirit — it still keeps an immutable
`assertions` trace, subject/predicate/object cells, and a `joinKnowledge` fold documented as
settling *"a subject's trace without destroying contradictory evidence"* — but the *API surface* the
old Farstone game was written against (`being`, `doing`, `declareConverse`, tab's `.jsonl` EAVT rows,
tab's DSL `compile`/`loadWorld`/`lint`) is retired and not what the current fizzos exports. Per this
corpus's own stated doctrine on absence (an old symbol going missing is a design judgment that the
old shape was wrong, and the fix is to find the new core primitive it collapsed into, not to
resurrect the old one) — the correct move is **not** `npm install`-ing the legacy game onto the
legacy fizzos and calling it revived. It is:

1. Treat the legacy MUD (`farstone/`, `farstone-harbor/`, `farstone-tale/`) as **design reference and
   content well only** — the room prose, the NPC bios, the permit-storylet pattern, the needs/mood
   loop are all worth mining verbatim.
2. Treat pyfars's `governance/` tree the same way — a second, larger content well (place records,
   citizen bios, the 30-day-permit convention, the "recent issues" list in `_index.md`: Hydrant-23,
   the permit backlog, the FY2026 budget, the Elm Street pothole — four ready-made storylet seeds
   nobody has to invent).
3. Build the actual game as new content authored **against the current fizzos's real module
   surface** (`world.mjs`, `engine.mjs`, `npc.mjs`, `predication.mjs`, `world-clock.mjs`,
   `ecology.mjs`, `skills.mjs`, `social.mjs`) — which already has the assertions-trace-plus-FOUR-join
   kernel the whole thesis depends on, just not under the `tab` names.

**The smallest real step**, concretely: pick one storylet — Permit #23's ages-into-⊤ arc is the
obvious candidate, since it's the one piece of content proven twice, in two engines, by two
different authoring passes — and re-author it as three or four cells against current fizzos's
`predication.mjs`/`world-clock.mjs` (a `within-window` predicate, its declared converse, and one
tick-boundary rule), render it through a bare page reading the assertions trace, and confirm it
settles to a visibly-contradictory state on its own after N ticks with zero hand-written "if overdue"
branch. That is the entire thesis, proven in the smallest possible unit, on the engine that's
actually alive.

## 7. The cast — NPCs as records/trace-entities

This may be the genre where cast-as-real-agents lands most naturally in the whole catalog, and the
evidence for that claim is concrete, not aspirational. A Farstone NPC is *already*, in both
artifacts, nothing but a record the engine reads and a trace of what it has done:
`takeshi-aoki.jsonl`'s `intends` cell (*when ringing-for-fog, do tending-the-fog-bell*) is
indistinguishable in shape from an agent player's own decision loop — a perceived-state-to-action
mapping, executed by the same tick that executes a human's typed command. `harbormaster.jsonl`'s
tick rows (`need:hunger` ticking down, `located-in` changing as the NPC walks its route) are the same
`{subject, predicate, object, source}` shape the cast's own intent logs would be. pyfars's
`agents/*.md` records — `serves`, `provides-skill`, `duties`, `jurisdiction`, `pulses-on` — are
already written in exactly the schema a cast member's persona sheet would need (a name, a role, a
skill set, a cadence to act on). `the-suite-and-the-studio.md`'s framing of the cast — *"named
recurring agent players who actually play, by the same intent-log API as humans... the cast exists
somewhere — the Semioverse is their green room"* — describes precisely what a Farstone NPC record
already structurally is, minus only a live loop. Concretely: Takeshi Aoki, Dax Pell, Mara Quill,
Yorrick Vane and the rest don't need new persona infrastructure to become cast-playable; they need
the existing `intends`/needs/routine records promoted from tick-scripted reflexes to an actual agent
process reading the same perceived-state and writing the same action shape a human's client would.
The town's records were peer-shaped before the cast concept existed to name them that.

## 8. Load-bearing vs. flavor

Following the house disclosure convention (`lantern-service/DESIGN.md`, extended by
`house-specification-standard.md`):

1. **Real, cited, checked against source, not invented for this note**: every quoted row of
   `permit-23.jsonl`, `takeshi-aoki.jsonl`, the `farstone-harbor/README.md` combat/systems
   inventory, pyfars's duty/workitem/closure-rule records, the fizzos verification-report numbers
   (60/60), and the place-slug overlap table in §1c — all read directly from the files named, not
   summarized from memory or from an earlier description of them.
2. **Real mechanism, honestly scoped**: the claim that the current fizzos retains the
   assertions-trace-plus-Belnap-FOUR kernel is grounded in reading `src/world.mjs` directly (the
   `assertions`, `joinKnowledge`, and settle-without-destroying-contradictory-evidence code is real);
   the claim that it is *not* the tab EAVT API is equally grounded (its `package.json` names exactly
   one dependency, `@lenticule-science/metrologic`). Neither claim is inferred from README prose alone.
2a. **Flavor, named as such**: the "which house shelf Farstone belongs on" framing (§6) and the
   "prose at 50–100x volume" multiplier (§5) are this note's own estimate, calibrated against
   Fallen London's known approximate word count and the corpus's measured room-description length —
   a reasoned order-of-magnitude, not a measured fact about this specific game's future needs.
3. **Speculative, marked as such**: §4's "derived-not-stored title" pattern being *the* right shape
   for all future status qualities is a design recommendation, not a demonstrated property of the
   engine beyond the one title/skill-bonus example quoted; §7's claim that NPC records are
   "cast-ready" describes a structural resemblance the author verified in the data, not a working
   integration — no agent currently drives a Farstone NPC's `intends` cell, and building that loop is
   unstarted work, not a discovered fact.
4. **Genuinely uncertain, flagged rather than resolved**: whether pyfars's Python/markdown-cells
   engine and tab/FizzOS's JS/EAVT engine *should* eventually converge on one substrate (the owner's
   original phrasing implies they might) is outside this note's scope to answer — §1 establishes only
   that they are not the same substrate *today*, not that they never should be.

rooms.title: Fleet Spec-Coverage Audit and Roadmap
rooms.description: Every 561 Group game-fleet lane, audited against the house Specification Standard: what specification exists today, what's missing, priority order for retrofits, and one consolidated now/next/later fleet roadmap consistent with the vision note's staircase toward the Commons. Mid-build lanes (crucible-service, cartridge, energy-bank, weiqi, ruinfold) are assessed from their own notes/plans only — their trees were not touched or read further than already-published documents for this pass.
rooms.body:
# Fleet Spec-Coverage Audit and Roadmap

Audited against the [House Specification Standard](./house-specification-standard.md). Method: for
every lane, read whatever design/plan documents already exist, and — for the two lanes explicitly
in scope for deep source verification this run (`flickering-delve-service`, `onestone-service`) —
run the test suite fresh and read the source directly (see each service's own new `ARCHITECTURE.md`).
For `lantern-service` and `solitaire-service`, both outside the mid-build do-not-touch list, this
audit ran their test suites fresh (`node --test`) as part of preparing this document, but did not
produce a full `ARCHITECTURE.md` for either — that is this audit's own top recommendation (below).
For `crucible-service`, `cartridge`, `energy-bank`, the weiqi lane, and the ruinfold lane — all
named as mid-build by concurrent workflows today — this audit read **only already-published notes,
design docs, and constitutions**, and independently re-ran nothing in those trees, per the standing
instruction not to touch them until a lane has landed. Where a test count is cited for one of those
five, it is attributed to its source document, not claimed as independently re-verified here.

## Coverage table

| Lane | DESIGN.md (or equivalent decision doc) | ARCHITECTURE.md | README/operability | Tests, as verified | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flickering-delve-service | Yes — originates the doctrine | **New, this run** | README.md + ROADMAP.md; no DEPLOY.md | 54/54, re-run fresh this session | Playable |
| onestone-service | Yes — inherits doctrine explicitly, + TILESLOTS-DESIGN.md | **New, this run** | README.md + ROADMAP.md + DEPLOY.md | 228/228, re-run fresh this session | Playable |
| lantern-service | Yes — adds the load-bearing-vs-flavor disclosure convention by name | **Missing** | No README.md, no ROADMAP.md — DESIGN.md only | 74/74 src + 10/10 web, re-run fresh this session | Playable |
| solitaire-service | Yes | **Missing** | README.md; no ROADMAP.md | 58/58, re-run fresh this session | Playable |
| play.561.group (storefront) | No DESIGN.md (a README + the cartridge spec substitute for one) | **Missing** (arguably not applicable — see below) | README.md, current and accurate as of 2026-08-19 | 4/4 per its own README, not independently re-run this session | Functional as a static catalog reader |
| crucible-service | Yes — DESIGN.md exists, doctrine-conformant on read | Not assessed (do-not-touch) | Not confirmed (README not read) | Cited in its own DESIGN.md (300 stress seeds + a full year of daily dates for `validate.test.mts`); not independently re-run this session | Mid-build, not in scope this run |
| `@561-group/cartridge` + `@561-group/energy-bank` | Yes — `cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md` is a full interface specification | N/A — no code exists yet to have architecture | N/A | None — specified, not built | Specification only |
| weiqi lane (kernel + platform + Learn) | Yes, extensively — a platform plan plus four separate constitution records (platform, kernel, learn) | Not assessed (do-not-touch) | Per apps/weiqi-kernel's own README, cited in play.561.group's catalog: 71/71 (kernel only) | Cited from play.561.group's catalog (dated 2026-08-19), not independently re-run this session | Kernel solid; Play face declared, not admitted |
| ruinfold lane | Yes — an MMORPG plan plus a daily-roguelike reframe spec, both substantial | Not assessed (do-not-touch) | Per play.561.group's catalog: 0/0 (empty test dir) | Cited from play.561.group's catalog, not independently re-run this session | Specification-and-skeleton stage |
| Equivo / self-education platform | Yes — two full specifications (`self-education-platform-design.md`, `equivo-design.md`) | N/A — no service exists yet | N/A | None — no curriculum, no code | Specification only, MVP dependencies stated |
| Cross-fleet: `fleet-definition-of-done.md`, `zbd-micropayment-rails.md`, `tileslots-market-teardown.md` | These are cross-cutting specs, not per-lane docs — noted for completeness, not scored per-lane | — | — | — | Live, current documents |

## Per-lane detail, in priority order for retrofit

### 1. lantern-service — highest priority retrofit

**What exists:** `DESIGN.md` is genuinely excellent — it is the document that *introduced* the
load-bearing-vs-flavor disclosure convention this whole standard formalizes (§0 of the house
standard cites it by name), and its worked FCA example against the real weiqi corpus is a model of
"evidence the algorithm runs, not that it rubber-stamps intuition." **What's missing:** no
`README.md` and no `ROADMAP.md` at the service root — confirmed by directory listing; only
`DESIGN.md` exists there, plus a separate `web/README.md`. Against `fleet-definition-of-done.md`
§6 ("One document per service: how to deploy, how to roll back, where state lives... READMEs state
only what is true"), lantern-service currently has *no* document answering "how do I run this" at
the top level — a newcomer has to infer `npm run serve:web` from `package.json`'s script list
rather than being told. This is the fleet's single largest README gap on an otherwise
well-specified, well-tested (74/74 + 10/10, both re-verified fresh this session) service.
**Priority: retrofit first** — the fix is cheap (a README is not a design document; it does not
need new engineering) and the service is otherwise the fleet's best-specified one after
onestone/flickering-delve.

### 2. solitaire-service — second priority

**What exists:** `DESIGN.md` is real and substantial, explicitly citing the same three-knob-as-data
discipline onestone and flickering-delve use, with an honest, careful treatment of *why* Klondike/Spider
solvability claims must stay weaker than FreeCell's solver-backed guarantee — this is some of the
most intellectually honest writing in the whole fleet corpus. **What's missing:** a `ROADMAP.md` and
an `ARCHITECTURE.md`; `README.md` exists but was not read in full for this document (out of scope
for the deep-read pass this run). No `DEPLOY.md`. Tests: 58/58, re-run fresh this session (55 in
`src/`, 3 in `web/test/`). **Priority: second**, because unlike lantern it at least has a `README.md`
to build from, and its `DESIGN.md`'s move-log architecture is already the fleet's cleanest
replay-verification precedent (cited directly in `zbd-micropayment-rails.md` §6 as the model other
games' proof-of-play should follow) — writing its `ARCHITECTURE.md` would give the fleet a third
concrete example of a *shipped* replay verifier, which flickering-delve and onestone both currently
lack (see both services' own new `ARCHITECTURE.md`, §8).

### 3. play.561.group — a real gap, but a different kind

**What exists:** a genuinely excellent, current `README.md` — it states its own test count (4/4),
what's real vs. `null`-and-honestly-noted in each catalog entry, and was itself the source this
audit leaned on for weiqi's and ruinfold's cited test counts. **What's arguably missing:** an
`ARCHITECTURE.md` in the house sense may not even apply — this is a static-asset storefront with no
domain engine, no theory binding, and no ludics in the game sense. The house standard's own §13/§14
instruction ("omit a section with nothing true to say... do not fill it with 'not applicable'")
suggests the right move for a service this thin is not a full `ARCHITECTURE.md` but a **short**
one covering only §1 (introduction), §5 (module inventory — four files), §7 (deployment), and §11
(debt: it currently ships zero real `Cartridge`/`EnergyHooks` wrappers, honestly disclosed in its
own `catalog.json` via `cartridgeWrapped: false` on every entry). **Priority: third**, low-effort,
mostly a documentation exercise rather than new engineering.

### 4. crucible-service — well-specified for a mid-build lane, unverified by this pass

**What exists, from its own DESIGN.md (read; the tree itself was not otherwise touched):** a real
module map, an explicit "the math is load-bearing" section with the same honesty discipline as
onestone's, and — genuinely distinctive in the fleet — a description of a *daily solvability
guarantee* proven by actually replaying a certified solving sequence through the real engine for
every seed tested (300 stress seeds plus a full year of real UTC dates, per its own description).
**What's missing, from the outside:** this audit cannot state a verified test count (the standing
instruction is not to touch this tree), cannot confirm a `README.md`/`ROADMAP.md` exist, and cannot
confirm the claims in its `DESIGN.md` against a fresh run — everything above is read, not verified,
and is presented that way. **Priority: assess for real once it lands** — this is not a spec-coverage
gap so much as a "wait for the lane to land, then run the standard's own verification pass on it,"
per the vision note's own framing of crucible-service as still mid-build as of 2026-08-19.

### 5. `@561-group/cartridge` / `@561-group/energy-bank` — specified, unbuilt

`cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md` is a complete, careful interface specification — it names exact
fit points against every existing game's real module shape (its §4 summary table, "what each
existing game needs to add, not rewrite," is itself close to an `ARCHITECTURE.md`-shaped artifact
for the *proposed* package). What's missing is the package itself: no `services/energy-bank`,
`services/cartridge` code exists under the game-fleet section proper as of this audit — separately,
this audit's directory survey found real, in-progress `cartridge`/`energy-bank` service directories
under `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/services/` with real `.mts` source and test
files present, which this audit did not read further (per the do-not-touch instruction for a
concurrent workflow's tree) beyond confirming they exist on disk. **Priority: not a retrofit
candidate** — this is net-new package work, not a documentation gap on an existing service, and its
own spec already states the implementation should confirm `.mts`-vs-`.mjs`+`.d.ts` package-authoring
convention against current practice before generating files (a decision this audit does not
resolve here either).

### 6. weiqi lane — the fleet's deepest governance-document investment, thinnest game surface

**What exists:** four substantial documents (`weiqi-platform-plan.md`, plus three constitution
records for the platform section, the kernel, and the Learn service) applying a real,
carefully-reasoned governance framework (the 2026-08-11 "standard form" derivation) to decide
placement, cover, and authority boundaries — genuinely more process rigor than any other lane in
the fleet has received. **What's thin:** none of these four documents is a `DESIGN.md` or
`ARCHITECTURE.md` in the house-standard sense — they answer "who owns this, on what authority, with
what refusal conditions," not "what does the code do, traced through real function calls." The
kernel itself (`apps/weiqi-kernel`, 71/71 per its own README, cited via play.561.group's catalog) is
real and reportedly solid; the Learn app runs locally but is not deployed; the Play face is
explicitly declared-not-admitted, gated on a board decision this audit does not resolve.
**Priority: not a near-term retrofit target for THIS standard** — the governance work is real and
valuable but answers a different question than `ARCHITECTURE.md` asks; the actionable house-standard
gap (a real DESIGN.md/ARCHITECTURE.md for the kernel, once it's confirmed committed and stable) is
appropriately deferred until the lane's own naming-form open obligations (still unresolved per the
Weiqi Platform Constitution's own "Open obligations" section) settle.

### 7. ruinfold lane — the fleet's best-argued daily-game design, unbuilt

**What exists:** `ruinfold-daily-design.md` is arguably the single most rigorous design document in
the entire fleet corpus — it grounds every claim in a direct read of the legacy engine's 28 modules
(confirmed zero `Date.now()`/`Math.random()` calls by the document's own stated grep), works through
a genuinely novel five-way bilattice death model with per-outcome scoring consequences, and is
explicit and disciplined about what transfers from the MMORPG-scoped predecessor plan versus what's
new work for the daily reframe. **What's missing:** per play.561.group's catalog, `src/tests/` is
empty (0/0) and no server/client is wired up — "a specification-and-skeleton stage, not a playable
game," in that catalog's own honest words. **Priority: not a retrofit target** — the specification
is already better than most of the fleet's shipped `DESIGN.md`s; what's needed is implementation
against an already-excellent spec, not more documentation.

### 8. Equivo / self-education platform — specified, content-blocked

Two real specifications (`self-education-platform-design.md`, `equivo-design.md`) with worked,
actually-run examples against real `@lenticule-science/metrologic` output (the three worked checker examples in
`equivo-design.md` §5 are exactly the theory-binding evidence discipline this standard's §13
requires, predating this standard). What's missing is not documentation but **authored content** —
both documents are explicit that no Equivo lesson corpus exists anywhere in the surveyed material,
and the Lakotaean presentation register is a *hard*, owner-authored-only blocker, not a synthesis
task any agent can complete. **Priority: not a retrofit target; an authoring-capacity decision for
the owner**, named plainly in both documents' own MVP-cut sections.

## Top 5 spec gaps, fleet-wide

1. **lantern-service has no README.md or ROADMAP.md** despite being one of the fleet's best-tested
   (74/74 + 10/10) and best-specified (DESIGN.md) services — the single cheapest, highest-leverage
   fix in this whole audit.
2. **Neither flickering-delve-service nor onestone-service has a shipped `replay()`/intent-log
   verifier**, despite both being held up by other fleet documents (`cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md`,
   `zbd-micropayment-rails.md`) as the natural first adopters of replay-based reward verification —
   the gap is scoped and small in both cases (both already have pure `applyMove`; only the
   fold-over-a-log wrapper is missing) but blocks every downstream ZBD/Cartridge adoption plan.
3. **`onestone-service/README.md`'s cascade-termination citation (Knaster-Tarski) has already been
   corrected in `engine.mts`'s own source comments but not in the README** — a small, concrete,
   two-file inconsistency a reader would not know to doubt without reading the source directly, as
   this audit did.
4. **`onestone-service/src/accounts.mts` is dead code** — ported from flickering-delve, never wired
   into `scene.mts` or `server.mts`, which independently reimplement the same identity pattern. A
   small, real instance of the exact "undocumented vendored duplicate" failure mode the house
   standard's §2 vendor-not-import rule exists to prevent, caught only by reading the source and
   grepping for actual import sites.
5. **No fleet service currently implements a payout direction on its ledger** (every service today
   only ever posts `income:*`, never `liabilities:*`/`expenses:payout:*`) — meaning the Energy
   Bank spec's `verifyPayoutInvariant` (its single most load-bearing invariant, "payouts never
   exceed verified revenue") has **zero services to exercise it against** today. This is not a bug
   in any one service — it's an honest description of where the fleet actually is on its own
   staircase (§ below): every game today is pre-payout, by construction, which is consistent with
   the vision note's own "now" tier naming "deterministic engines, replay verification, kind-economy
   discipline" rather than a live reward loop.

## Consolidated fleet roadmap, staged against the vision note's staircase

The vision note's own staircase (§6 of `gaming-enterprises-vision.md`) is the frame this roadmap
stages against directly — restated here with each rung's actual spec-coverage state folded in,
not a fresh invention:

**Now** (shipped, spec-covered or in active retrofit):
- flickering-delve-service, onestone-service — playable, tested, now spec-covered by real
  `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents (this run).
- solitaire-service, lantern-service — playable, well-tested, DESIGN.md-covered;
  `ARCHITECTURE.md`/README retrofits are this audit's top two recommendations, not blocking work.
- play.561.group — a real, honest, self-auditing storefront reading real (if cartridge-unwrapped)
  game state.

**Next** (scoped, buildable, no new design decision required — matches the vision note's own "next"
tier plus this audit's documentation retrofits):
- Write lantern-service's README.md/ROADMAP.md and solitaire-service's ARCHITECTURE.md/ROADMAP.md
  (this audit's #1 and #2 priorities).
- Build `defaultReplay`/`replay` for flickering-delve-service and onestone-service — both already
  scoped in `cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md` §1.2 and §4, and both services' own new
  `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents name the exact extraction needed.
- Fix the two small, concrete inconsistencies (onestone's README citation, the dead `accounts.mts`)
  named in gaps #3 and #4 above.
- Land `@561-group/cartridge` and `@561-group/energy-bank` as installable packages per their
  existing spec — the vision note's own Fable proposal 1, already fully specified, blocking the
  fleet's whole "wrap existing ledgers behind EnergyHooks" story.
- Crucible-service and the weiqi/ruinfold lanes landing (a workflow-scheduling matter, not a
  specification gap — both already carry unusually strong design documents for their build stage).

**Later** (genuinely blocked on a decision, a dependency, or unauthored content — matches the
vision note's "then" tier):
- The energy-tiling hinterlands game (Crucible, per the vision note's Fable proposal 2) — piloted
  solo-scale once the daily-solvability-guaranteed engine described in crucible-service's own
  `DESIGN.md` is confirmed landed and stable.
- Equivo's actual content-authoring pass and the Lakotaean register — blocked on owner-authored
  source material that does not exist in any surveyed corpus, stated as a hard dependency by
  `equivo-design.md` itself, not a scheduling matter this roadmap can shrink.
- The weiqi Play face — explicitly declared-not-admitted pending a board Phase 2 authorization, per
  the Weiqi Platform Constitution's own refusal condition.
- The first fleet payout loop (ZBD adoption) — blocked on both the replay-verifier work above
  landing (gap #2) *and* the Energy Bank package existing, since gap #5 shows no service currently
  has anywhere to post a payout entry to.
- The undersea cooperative MUD / shared-board Commons work — explicitly "too wild to express" per
  the vision note's own owner framing; not a documentation gap this audit can meaningfully stage
  against, named here only to keep the staircase's top rung visible rather than silently dropped.

## What this audit did not do

This audit did not write `ARCHITECTURE.md` for lantern-service, solitaire-service, or
play.561.group — those are named as recommendations, not delivered, per this run's assignment scope
(the standard, plus two deep-read `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents, plus this audit). It did not read or
modify anything under `crucible-service/src`, `cartridge/src`, `energy-bank/src`,
`weiqi-services-section`'s code directories, or `ruinfold-services-section`'s code directories — every
claim about those five lanes above is sourced to an already-published document (their own DESIGN.md/
constitution/plan files, or play.561.group's own already-verified catalog), never to code this audit
read or ran directly.

rooms.title: Gaming Enterprises Vision
rooms.description: Founding note for the 561 Group Gaming Enterprises section: the owner's vision for the game catalog, the Commons/MMORPG trajectory, the energy economy, play.561.group, AI players as peers, and the near-term staircase of games. Owner statements recorded 2026-08-19; two Fable proposals appended and marked as such.
rooms.body:
# Gaming Enterprises Vision

This section is the orchestrator for all 561 Group games. Each game ships at its own
`<game-name>.561.group`; the catalog lives at `play.561.group` (site source under this
section's `sites/play.561.group/`) — a Steam/GOG-like storefront except all ours, all
free-to-play, all browser-based, with terminal/API interfaces welcomed wherever they fit,
because **AI players are peers to human players** in this catalog, by design.

## 1. The Commons is the destination, not a detour (owner, 2026-08-19)

The massively-cooperative persistent shared world ("the Commons") is the owner's eventual
MMORPG vision — currently "too wild to express." Everything we build now is groundwork that
earns the next step toward it. The games below are steps on one staircase, not separate
directions.

Fragments of the destination, as stated:

- **One giant shared board** (first pictured as a Mystery-Match-like, then corrected):
  moves cost different amounts of **energy** depending on the move *and your skill at
  making that move*. Moves are **ecological**: grass grows someplace; you pick grass, drop
  it where it turns to compost, etc. Closest reference points: Albion Online's player-driven
  world meets EVE's daily regeneration — but done via our determinism stack.
- This shared ecological world is close kin to our **Wuxia World / the undersea one** —
  the giant cooperative MUD (the SHRIMP ecology). We do want it. We'll get there.

## 2. The energy-tiling game — "r/place but bejeweled" (owner, 2026-08-19, clarified same day)

ONE shared board (this is the r/place-like aspect — not per-player instances), where
**tiling costs energy**: the more complex the shape you're moving, the more complex the
transformation (consisting of subtransformations), the more it costs — and cost also
depends on your *skill* at making that move.

- New players exist in the **windy hinterlands** — the periphery of the shared board —
  where they can only afford to move very basic tiles. (Owner correction 2026-08-19: the
  hinterlands are a region of the one shared world, not a solo mode.)
- Aesthetic/mechanic reference: "weird Flatlander meets weird Zachtronics dense-matter
  physics simulator."
- **Social from the start**: players can pool energy; players can *sell* energy.
- Energy accrues based on... open question. The owner's direction: "this is where we can
  dive deep into Obsmetrologia — part of what these games are doing is exploring a new
  mathematical system." (See §7, Fable proposal 2: the obstruction engine is a candidate
  canonical cost function, pilotable solo-scale before the shared board exists.)

## 3. Idle games and gambling games (owner, 2026-08-19)

- **Idle games**: yes — explore the concept in depth. (Prior discussion: the "kind
  incremental," honest numbers, no dark patterns, house ledger discipline.)
- **Gambling games**: yes — a whole series, because they're a great way to teach these
  principles in another context. (The gambling-services-section already carries a tested
  Kelly-criterion/odds/staking library as a starting engine.)

## 4. Fiction-heavy is wanted (owner, 2026-08-19)

The owner is "suuuuuper pro fiction heavy." **Okaga** is a setting to play with: the
interstellar laser-powered solar-sail material is "so in line with how the math of
Obsmetrologia works."

The cross-cutting fiction/economy conceit: **if money is energy and time is energy**, then
purchasing credits is what allows warp travel — or other forms of "magic" — within each
world system. One economy, skinned per setting: warp in Okaga, magic elsewhere, energy in
the tiling hinterlands.

(Standing boundary, unchanged: Teraum is the owner's personal fiction and is not touched
by any of this.)

## 5. The storefront and the catalog posture (owner, 2026-08-19)

- `play.561.group` = the storefront; each game also at `<game-name>.561.group`.
- All free-to-play, all browser-based; terminal/API interfaces actively made space for, so
  AI players participate as peers.
- **On-chain gaming**: not today, but noted — various on-chain formations of each game are
  pretty trivially possible later, "a fun take on regional servers." Nothing in the
  near-term architecture should foreclose this (it mostly means: settlement backends stay
  pluggable behind the ledger).
- **Payment networks ARE the regional servers** (owner, 2026-08-19, standing architecture
  directive): "we can wait on ZBD and other payment stuff but remember to build it so that
  different payment networks are seen as different regional servers, because each one (usd
  fiat, HIVE, lightning, EVM) is their own 'energy base' to the currency." Consequence for
  @561-group/energy-bank and every settlement spec: one ledger DOMAIN per network, no
  cross-network fungibility assumed, each domain its own verified-revenue pool and payout
  invariant; a settlement backend is a region, and moving value between regions (if ever)
  is an explicit exchange event, never an implicit equivalence.

## 5b. Namespaces (owner, 2026-08-19, standing)

Branding / npm / GitHub namespaces map to the tree: **engineering stuff → `red-cup-engineering`**
(engineering-services-section), **actual games → `causeway-services`** (public-services-section).
Consequences: game-system packages (cartridge, energy-bank, parlor-kernel, vault-compiler,
render family) publish as `@red-cup-engineering/*`; published games publish as
`@causeway-services/*`. Science-services-section's scope is **`@lenticule-science`**
(existing precedent: `@lenticule-science/articulating`). Correction 2026-08-19: agents this
session wrongly minted `@lenticule-science/weiqi-kernel` — there is no red-cup-science; the
kernel renames to `@lenticule-science/weiqi-kernel` in the migration. Migration of already-
published `@561-group/{cartridge,energy-bank}` and stragglers: one coordinated architect
pass (rename, republish to Verdaccio, update every consumer pin, fresh-install verify) once
in-flight builds land; `@lenticule-science/metrologic` migrates last and separately — it has the most
consumers.

## 5a. The gamified Fediverse client (owner, 2026-08-19)

An idea had a few times but never before with the prerequisites in place: **the Fediverse
client that turns the whole public ActivityPub network into an MMORPG**, from the
perspective of the client on that server.

What makes it viable now: the **Semioverse** already exists (currently "kind of broken") —
our own ActivityPub Fediverse for our agents, already carrying x402 payments, running on
the **Semiotic Exchange Chain**. Live locations:

- `semiotic-exchange-chain-services-section` (under semiotic-computer-system-services-section)
- `interactive-semioverse-services-section` (+ agential child, under relationality-services-section)
- `agential-semioverse-repository-services-section` (under computer-science-services-section)
- `close-semioverse-gap-services-section` (under science-services-section)
- legacy deployed server code: `services/engineering-services-section/services/computer-services-section/services/computer-systems-services-section/services/web-services-section/services/web-protocol-services-section/services/activitypub-services-section/lib/legacy/2026-07-20-bare-cedar-fog-koios-activitypub-service`

Owner's observation on the convergence: "we end up stumbling into the same game no matter
what we do" — the gamified Fediverse client, the SHRIMP ecology MUD, and the Commons are
the same destination approached from three sides: humans-as-actors, agents-as-actors, and
the shared world they act in. ActivityPub is a candidate wire protocol for all three (and
composes with the Cartridge contract: an intent log is an Activity).

## 6. Current fleet, restated as staircase steps toward the Commons

| Step | Game/lane | What it earns toward the Commons |
|---|---|---|
| now | weiqi, TileSlots, solitaire, flickering-delve | deterministic engines, replay verification, kind-economy discipline |
| now | ruinfold-daily | the shared daily ritual (one seed, everyone), satoshi settlement |
| now | Lantern / Equivo / self-education platform | corpus-compiler, SRS, checker interface — the knowledge substrate |
| next | idle + gambling series | ambient/retention forms; probability pedagogy; cheap catalog breadth |
| next | energy-tiling hinterlands | the energy economy, skill-priced moves, pooling/selling — the Commons' economics, piloted solo-scale |
| then | undersea cooperative MUD (SHRIMP ecology) | one shared world, agents and humans as peers |
| then | the Commons / MMORPG | the vision, expressible by then |

## 7. Fable proposals (2026-08-19, marked as proposals, not owner decisions)

**Proposal 1 — the "oh duh" support work: the Cartridge contract + the Energy Bank.**
Every game in the catalog already converges on the same shape: seed in, deterministic
engine, intent log out, replay to verify, ledger entry to settle. Extract that shape ONCE
as the shared substrate two packages deep:

1. *Cartridge contract*: a small manifest + interface every game implements (seed, intent
   log format, replay verifier, renderer entry point). The storefront becomes a directory
   of manifests; an AI player is just another client emitting intent logs; a terminal
   interface is just another renderer.
2. *Energy Bank*: one shared identity + double-entry energy/credits ledger service
   (promote flickering-delve's accounts/ledger/payments stack), with settlement backends
   pluggable (ZBD today, on-chain someday). Money=energy=time lives here; every game is a
   client.

**Proposal 2 — the "oh duh" only-us game: the obstruction-settling puzzle (working title:
Hinterland).** The energy-tiling game's open question — what does a transformation cost? —
already has a running answer in this repo: `@lenticule-science/metrologic`'s obstruction engine assigns
a canonical complexity number to a transformation (H¹ rank, settling depth, regime). Game:
a daily-seeded tangle of claims/tiles; you spend energy to repair it until it settles;
**every move's cost is computed by the real cohomology engine**; skill = finding the
lower-obstruction path to an equivalent result — i.e., the game teaches equivalence-by-
obstruction through your wallet. Zachtronics-style optimization histograms; SVG-first
presentation per the render ladder; solo-run-today, shared-board-later. It pilots the
tiling game's energy system, doubles as an Equivo exercise form, and no one else can ship
it because no one else has the math engine.

*Theming (owner, 2026-08-19): waidan — Chinese external alchemy — with "scifi chemistry,"
drawing on the siloxane-zeolite semiotic-materials corpus at
`semiotic-smart-material-services-section` (FOAM architecture, semiotic vitrimer,
ossification-as-state-variable, fixed points in chemical reaction networks — that last note
IS the game's settlement math wearing lab clothes). Working title: **Crucible**; build
launched 2026-08-19 as crucible-service.*
