rooms.title: Sierra LucasArts Lineage Brief
rooms.description: Owner brief 2026-08-19: the classic-studio lineage wave — an Impressions-style finite-scenario city builder with Dawn of Man resource management and Indigenous American campaigns; the Sierra/LucasArts catalog audit; Anvil of Dawn and Obsidian revivals; point-and-click mystery; and the question 'what would these studios make if they survived to today?'
rooms.body:
# Sierra / LucasArts Lineage Brief

Owner statements, 2026-08-19, recorded faithfully; design work fans out from here.

## 1. The city builder (flagship of this wave)

- Genre memory: **Zeus / Poseidon / Caesar** — the Sierra-published city builders (built by
  Impressions Games): finite scenarios, campaign structure, win conditions per mission.
- But with resource management closer to **Dawn of Man**: material flows, seasons,
  survival pressure, technology moving through time — not the abstract walker-loops of the
  Impressions engine.
- **Daily challenges: yes** (house daily-seed pattern applies).
- **Campaigns are different Indigenous North and South American cultures, moving through
  time.** [Ringleader note, standing discipline: this inherits the house honest-absence
  rule established in the Equivo/platform docs for the Lakotaean register — no fabricated
  cultural content, real sources cited or gaps marked plainly as gaps; where a culture's
  own accounts are not in our hands, the design says *absent* rather than inventing.]
- **First campaign: Lakota** (owner, same day): "I'm Lakota and encourage you to use
  whatever scholarship available, that can be our first campaign to prove the concept."
  So the proof-of-concept campaign is designed from real scholarship plus the owner's own
  corpus (the Lakotaean-metaphysics material in the theory sections — which the owner
  holds to be the same mathematics as obsmetrologia/relationality/semiotics, meaning the
  campaign's mechanics can be theory-native rather than skinned). Subsequent cultures'
  campaigns remain owner decisions about scope and involvement.

## 2. The catalog audit

"What other games did Sierra, LucasArts put out, that we're not doing?" — a genre-by-genre
sweep of both catalogs (Sierra including its published studios like Impressions and
Dynamix; LucasArts) against the current 561 estate, to find the gaps worth wanting.

Named gap already: **no point-and-click mystery games** — "I loved those as a kid."

## 3. Revivals

- **Anvil of Dawn** (1995 first-person grid dungeon crawler): redo browser-based, "almost
  DOOM but... excursion shooters" [likely: **extraction** shooters — run in, get treasure,
  get out alive or lose it]. Note the house already owns the substrate lineage: abrash
  (software raycaster over a federated voxel world) and durante (first-playable Quake-like
  on abrash) in the legacy archive.
- **Obsidian** (1996, the Myst-like about a dreaming AI): "that shit? Seems very up our
  alley." A surreal first-person puzzle game about AI, made by a house whose own theory
  corpus is about machine cognition — the fiction can be load-bearing here.

## 4. The counterfactual

"What if these studios survived through to today: what would they make?" — a design
speculation exercise, grounded in each studio's actual design values (not their brands),
answered with 2026 reasoning the way the-suite-and-the-studio.md answered it for the
CD-suite form.

rooms.title: Studio Filing Reflection
rooms.description: After the owner's 2026-08-19 filing correction: what was misfiled and why, the corrected taxonomy, and the composition principle (Hoare contracts x Rendanheyi zero-distance) that should govern where game assets live from now on.
rooms.body:
# Studio Filing Reflection

## What was misfiled, and the correction (executed 2026-08-19)

My failure mode: **filing by proximity and recency instead of by kind** — creating new
top-level structure wherever I happened to be standing ("dribbling prose wherever is
nearby"), when the tree already had a place for every kind of thing:

| Kind | Wrong place (mine, now dissolved) | Right place (already existed) |
|---|---|---|
| Published playable games, storefront, vision/design notes | `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section` (invented at top level) | `public-.../public-computer-games-services-section` |
| Game systems (cartridge, energy-bank, engines) | `computer-gaming-systems-services-section` (invented; "services" that were actually apps) | `computer-systems-.../computer-game-system-services-section` |
| Science / theory / study of gaming | scattered | `science-.../game-science-services-section` |

Moves executed: cartridge + energy-bank → the systems home; all enterprise notes, the
estate map/inventory, the planned-game notes (now `notes/planned/`), and
`sites/play.561.group` → this games home; the invented sections deleted. A compatibility
symlink remains at the old `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section` path so
in-flight workflow caches resolve; remove it once nothing references it.

## The principle I violated (Hoare × Rendanheyi, from the governance corpus)

The governance note `2026-07-24-allosteric-governance-of-a-polycapcellular-union.md`
formalizes the settlement's standing law: **no office may act on another unit's execution
directly — only a contract, hook, schema, or checkpoint may** (Rendanheyi's zero-distance,
`ling-juli.md`: nothing stands between the person doing work and the user whose value it
creates). Applied to a game studio of one person and many agents:

1. **Games are the micro-enterprises.** Each published game faces users directly at its
   own subdomain. They live in the public games section because that's the user-facing
   membrane — zero distance.
2. **Gaming is the demand-inducer.** Each game's needs pull simple, atomic services into
   existence upstream — a seed deriver, a ledger, a replay harness, an FCA compiler, a
   raycaster. Those are the leaf nodes of the deep tree, and they live where their KIND
   lives (game systems under computer-game-system; math under math; transport under
   qwzspace), not where the game that wanted them happens to sit.
3. **Contracts are the only coupling.** The Cartridge interface, the energy-bank
   settlement interface, the vendored-copy-documented-as-port rule — these are Hoare-style
   pre/post contracts between enterprise and system. A game never reaches into a system's
   execution; a system never knows which game is calling. That is why card-game-systems,
   city-builder systems, QBN storylet compilers etc. must be built as **specializations
   and compositions of simpler upstream services** — composition is only possible when
   every unit is governed at its boundary.
4. **The tree is the proof.** If the filing is right, a stranger can walk from any
   published game down through its contracts to the atomic scripts it composed, and every
   step is a directory. If the filing is wrong, the theory is invisible no matter how good
   it is — "if we don't lay the bricks of the path out right, no one in the future will
   probably see it" (owner, 2026-08-19).

## Decisions taken (not deferred)

- **Cloud runners**: `gcloud` is configured on this box (account morgan.sennhauser@gmail.com,
  project `five-six-one-group-dev`, credentials present). Server-shaped services (ruinfold
  daily server, tidepool MUD, ActivityPub instance) target Google Cloud runners;
  static/game frontends stay on the Cloudflare path already reconned. cold-red-gate is the
  owner's small VPS — reserve it for things that want a stable tiny box (Verdaccio mirror,
  cron), not game traffic.
- **Planned games** are notes in `notes/planned/`, not stub "services." A game earns a
  `services/<name>-services-section/` here when real code exists.
- **New systems** (storylet compiler, city-builder simulation kernel, render family
  recovery) go under `computer-game-system-services-section/services/` from day one, as
  small composable packages with contracts — never as monoliths inside a game.

rooms.title: The Suite and the Studio
rooms.description: Design philosophy note: play.561.group as the CD-ROM game suite reborn, and what a solo-owner-plus-agent-fleet game corporation actually is under 2026 economics. Written by the session ringleader as design thought, at the owner's request; owner steers recorded, proposals marked.
rooms.body:
# The Suite and the Studio

Owner's prompt (2026-08-19): "we're recreating the game suites on CDs that the user knew
as a kid... a bunch of casino games on one CD, some point and click adventures on others...
lean into the fact that we're becoming a game design and development corporation, as one
part of our operations... helping us conceive of this using 2026 reasoning, because it's
all very new and strange and needs thought to understand."

## 1. What the CD suite actually was

Hoyle Card Games, the Microsoft Entertainment Pack, Chessmaster, the shareware "1000
Games" discs. Strip the nostalgia and their design properties were:

1. **A bounded collection.** You owned the whole thing. Finite, browsable, yours. The
   product was the shelf, not any single game on it.
2. **Finished games.** No servers, no patches, no live-ops treadmill. Done-ness was a
   virtue — the games worked identically in year five as on day one.
3. **One house's hand visible everywhere.** Hoyle's card backs and its recurring cast of
   fake opponents; the Entertainment Pack's shared chrome. Family resemblance across many
   small games was itself the brand.
4. **Portfolio economics.** No single game had to be a hit. Value = variety × a polish
   floor. The suite absorbed individual weakness.
5. **Trust by business model.** One-time purchase meant no dark patterns; you were the
   customer, not the product. The suite lived on the family computer as furniture —
   ambient, safe, returned-to for years.

What killed the form: the web and F2P economics atomized suites into individually
monetized SKUs with live-ops obligations. Modern casual gaming kept the *games* (solitaire,
casino, match-3 — literally our catalog) and discarded every trust property. The games
survived; the *shelf* died.

## 2. What 2026 lets the suite do that the CD could not

play.561.group is not a Steam/GOG storefront (correction to this section's own earlier
framing). Storefronts are unbounded aggregators of other people's goods. This is the
opposite: a bounded shelf of one house's finished games. The CD suite reborn — plus four
things plastic could never do:

- **One persistent economy across the shelf.** The CD suite had per-game high-score
  tables at best. The Energy Bank gives the whole shelf one wallet: energy earned in one
  game spendable in another, money=energy=time, skinned per setting (warp in Okaga, magic
  elsewhere). The suite becomes an economy, not a folder.
- **A shared daily ritual.** One "today" page: today's ruinfold dungeon, today's crucible
  tangle, today's weiqi problem. The CD suite's "what shall we play tonight" browsing
  moment, made daily and communal (same seeds for everyone).
- **The cast is real.** Hoyle shipped fake opponents with canned barks — and players
  loved them anyway; the cast was half the charm. We can ship the genuine article: named
  recurring agent players who actually play, by the same intent-log API as humans
  (peers-not-pets is already the architecture). Meeting the same opponent in weiqi and
  later at the card table is continuity no other studio can offer honestly. Between
  games, the cast exists somewhere — the Semioverse is their green room. This may be the
  single strongest differentiator the fleet owns.
- **Finished AND alive.** The games stay finished (deterministic, zero-dep, no patch
  treadmill — additions are content data, not code). The *world around them* is what
  lives: seeds rotate daily, the cast circulates, the economy flows. Done-ness and
  liveness stop being opposites.

And the trust property returns by a new mechanism: the CD earned trust through one-time
purchase; we earn it through **earn-only economics** — free-to-play where money flows
toward the player (satoshi payouts against verified replays) and never against them (no
wagering, no energy walls, no ads-to-continue).

*(Corrected 2026-08-19, conceding wilder-conceptions-01 item 1: this section originally
claimed the shelf could say "we pay you; you are never the product being sold." That
overclaims. The payout cycle balances on the ledger — that part is structural and
checkable — but something off the ledger pays for it, and in the owner's own stated model
that carrier is named: ads. The honest trust copy is:* **"We sell ads and share the
revenue with the players. We never take your money to play, never let you wager it, and
never pay out more than we verifiably earned."** *Still a sentence no incumbent F2P
catalog can adopt — revenue-sharing with players is the differentiator — and now it names
the carrier instead of hiding it. Every settlement flow gets a named carrier per the
Carrier Audit discipline, assigned to the house spec standard §8.)*

## 3. Shelves within the shelf

The owner's memory is of *distinct* CDs — the casino disc, the adventure disc. So the
suite organizes as shelves, not genre tags:

| Shelf | Games | The CD it reincarnates |
|---|---|---|
| The Card Table | solitaire, gambling/probability series | Hoyle Casino |
| The Puzzle Den | TileSlots, Crucible, flickering-delve | Entertainment Pack / puzzle discs |
| The Study | weiqi + Learn, Lantern, Equivo | Chessmaster / edutainment discs |
| The Deep | ruinfold daily, later the undersea MUD and the Commons | the MUD/BBS door-games lineage |
| The Stars (later) | Okaga-set games; credits-as-warp | the space-sim disc |

Each shelf gets its own register of the shared chrome — same frame, different felt.

## 4. The studio, reasoned as a 2026 corporation

What is a solo owner plus an agent fleet, as a company? Not a small version of a normal
studio — a structurally different animal:

1. **The scarce resource inverts.** Traditional studios ration engineering hours; design
   is cheap relative to implementation. Here implementation capacity is effectively
   unbounded and *design judgment is the bottleneck*. The rational org is a tiny taste
   core (the owner; the ringleader; the standing architect) gating an elastic build
   fleet. Every process should optimize for the quality of design decisions per owner-
   hour, not for build throughput.
2. **Portfolio beats lottery — now provably.** Studios bet big on few titles because dev
   cost is huge. When a finished small game costs roughly its design thought plus
   verification, the CD-suite strategy (many small, finished, polished, shared-substrate
   games) strictly dominates the hit-chasing strategy. The owner's instinct is the
   economically correct 2026 strategy, not nostalgia.
3. **Departments become properties.** QA is the adversarial-verify pass. Anti-cheat is
   replay determinism. Compliance is ethics-as-executable-tests. Localization/theming is
   the register system. What used to be headcount is now an invariant that either holds
   or fails a build. The corporation's org chart is a test suite.
4. **The employees inhabit the products.** The agents that build the games also play in
   them, as the cast. No prior company could put its workforce inside its catalog as
   characters. This collapses community management, NPC design, and QA playtesting into
   one ongoing fact: the studio *lives on its own shelf*.
5. **R&D and product are the same artifact.** Each game explores a piece of the house
   mathematics (the owner: "part of what these games are doing is exploring a new
   mathematical system"). Crucible's energy costs are computed by the obstruction engine;
   onestone's rigidity is Laman theory; Equivo grades by cohomology. The catalog is
   simultaneously a public lab notebook — a Bell Labs whose products are solitaire games.
   This means design depth and research depth are the same investment, which is why
   "deeper game design thought" and "deeper theory specification" converge on the same
   documents (the architect's §13/§14 mandate).
6. **Boundedness is the luxury good.** In an infinite-content medium, a finite,
   finished, trustworthy shelf is the differentiation. The CD suite was bounded by
   necessity; we choose boundedness as positioning.

## 5. Concrete design directives that fall out (proposals, for the owner)

1. **Shelf chrome**: one small shared UI frame around every game (title treatment,
   settings, energy meter, dark/light, the "today" strip) — the modern card back. Rides
   the cartridge contract; vendored per house doctrine, not live-imported.
2. **The Today page** as the suite's front door: every game's daily seed in one place;
   the catalog page is for browsing the shelves, the Today page is for the ritual.
3. **The cast, v1**: three to five named agent players with stable personas, playing
   real games via intent logs, starting on whichever lane lands multiplayer-shaped
   surfaces first (weiqi problems, ruinfold leaderboard, card table). Persona continuity
   across games from day one; Semioverse residency when its live instance exists.
4. **Done-ness definition per game**: shipped = complete + polished + no live-ops
   dependency + content pipeline documented. The architect's ARCHITECTURE.md roadmap
   appendix should carry a "finished means" line per game.
5. **Trust copy on the shelf itself**, stated plainly and testably: no wagering, no
   energy walls, no ads-to-continue, payouts only against verified play, odds published
   wherever chance exists.
6. **Suite continuity bible** (small!): the cast roster, the shelf registers, the
   energy-economy skins per setting — a reference so every lane's flavor decisions
   compound instead of drifting. Owned by the standing architect; kept to a few pages;
   explicitly not a vocabulary empire.

## 6. What this note changes operationally

- play.561.group copy and information architecture should shift from "storefront" to
  "shelf/suite" framing (catalog → shelves; add Today page when two or more daily games
  are live).
- The standing architect's mandate gains suite-level coherence review: chrome, cast,
  registers, done-ness lines.
- The cast becomes a real backlog item attached to the first multiplayer-shaped surface,
  not a someday-idea.

rooms.title: Three Marks
rooms.description: Branding reasoning pass for the gaming estate's three faces: Causeway Services (the public games shelf), Red Cup Engineering (game systems), Lenticule Science (game sciences). What each mark means, what each brand owns, what each must never do — proposals for the owner, grounded in what the tree already is.
rooms.body:
# Three Marks

The owner asked (2026-08-19) for a reasoning pass on branding the public gaming services
section, the internal game engineering section, and the internal game sciences section.
The finding up front: **we don't need to invent brands — we need to notice the ones the
tree already carries, because all three names accidentally-or-not describe their section's
actual function.** Branding here is the same move as the filing correction: stop inventing,
start reading what's there.

## 0. Why three brands and not one

One brand would collapse three audiences with incompatible needs. A player needs to trust
us fast; a builder needs contracts and composability; a reader of the theory needs
epistemic rigor. The Hoare × Rendanheyi doctrine already separates these as layers —
zero-distance user membrane, systems-by-contract, evidence — so the brand architecture is
just that doctrine made legible:

| Audience | Brand | Section | Namespace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Players | **Causeway** | public games (this section) | `@causeway-services` |
| Builders (human + agent) | **Red Cup** | game systems (engineering) | `@red-cup-engineering` |
| Readers / the field | **Lenticule** | game sciences (science) | `@lenticule-science` |

## 1. Causeway — the shelf players walk

**The image:** a causeway is stones laid across water so people can cross. It is public
infrastructure, walkable by anyone, built one stone at a time, and it connects islands.

**Why it's almost overdetermined for this catalog:** the house's games are stones —
*onestone*, *Farstone*, weiqi's stones on the board — and the destination the whole
staircase walks toward is water: Tidepool, the undersea MUD, the SEA of the SHRIMP
ecology, the Deep shelf. A causeway is exactly what play.561.group is: a laid path of
individual stones (games) that together let a stranger cross into our water. The CD-suite
thesis (the-suite-and-the-studio.md) gets a name: the shelf is the causeway.

**What the Causeway brand owns:** the shelf chrome (the modern card back), the Today page,
the trust copy — and the trust copy IS the brand: *"We sell ads and share the revenue with
the players. We never take your money to play, never let you wager it, and never pay out
more than we verifiably earned."* No wagering, no energy walls, published odds, earn-only.
Causeway is the only brand players ever need to see.

**What Causeway must never do:** ship a dark pattern (the executable-ethics tests are the
brand's enforcement arm); brand a system or a theory doc (those aren't its audience);
promise what the ledger can't prove.

**Voice:** warm, plain, a little wry — Kingdom-of-Loathing-adjacent humor is in-bounds on
the shelf (the Chutes & Ladders bot IS a die, and we say so). Never solemn, never salesy.

**Proposed marks:** wordmark "Causeway" with per-game titles as the stones ("a Causeway
game"). Games keep their own names and palettes — same card back, different felt.

## 2. Red Cup — the vessel that holds anything

**The image:** the red cup is the plainest vessel there is — sturdy, ubiquitous,
unembarrassed, and it holds whatever you pour into it. That is precisely what a game
*system* is under the house doctrine: a contract-shaped container indifferent to its
contents. The cartridge package is literally this image as software.

**What the Red Cup brand owns:** the systems under computer-game-system-services-section
(cartridge, energy-bank, parlor-kernel, vault-compiler, the render family) plus the wider
engineering substrate (fizzos, qwzspace, the ActivityPub server). Its brand artifacts are
READMEs, contracts, and invariants — the org chart that is a test suite.

**A real naming convention worth canonizing (it already exists):** Red Cup names its
*engines* after pioneers — Abrash (software 3D), Tsander (rocketry → wireframe engine),
Wheatstone (telegraphy → MUD client), Daleske, Arnold. Proposal: keep this as the house
rule — **engines carry pioneer names; packages carry plain nouns** (cartridge,
energy-bank, parlor-kernel). The pioneer name says "this is a deep system with a lineage";
the plain noun says "this is a vessel, use it." Both are Red Cup.

**What Red Cup must never do:** appear on a player-facing surface (the chrome is
Causeway's; a player should be able to love the shelf without ever learning the plumbing's
name); claim a theory result (cite Lenticule instead); publish a package whose README
states more than is true — the brand's reputation is exactly the reliability of its
contracts.

**Voice:** terse, precise, load-bearing. A Red Cup README reads like a datasheet with dry
wit permitted in comments.

## 3. Lenticule — the small lens

**The image:** a lenticule is a small lens — and an array of lenticules is how one image
shows differently from different angles. The house's deepest standing claim is exactly
this: *Obsmetrologia = relationality = semiotics = Lakotaean metaphysics — four lenses on
one mathematics.* The science brand's name already IS the doctrine.

**What the Lenticule brand owns:** game-science-services-section — ludics (both senses:
Caillois's play categories and Girard's ludics, and the house holds a real
Girard–Caillois correspondence note), the market teardowns, the regime taxonomy, the
theory bindings that every ARCHITECTURE.md §13 cites, weiqi's kernel-as-executable-
glossary program, the Lakota campaign sourcebook discipline. Proposed program name for
the game-study work specifically: **Lenticule Ludics**.

**What Lenticule must never do:** decorate. Its brand promise is the house's evidentiary
standard — recurrence-cited, honest-absence-preserving, "state only what is true." A
Lenticule citation in a game's design doc means *this mechanic is real mathematics*; the
brand dies the first time that's false. (The Equivo/vendor-a-copy overclaim caught by a
verifier this session is the exact failure mode; the correction discipline is the brand.)

**Voice:** the primary-source voice the theory corpus already has. No press-release
register, ever.

## 4. How the three marks touch

- **The colophon rule (proposal):** every shipped game may carry one quiet line on its
  about/credits surface — *"A Causeway game · Red Cup systems · Lenticule mathematics"* —
  and that is the ONLY place the three marks co-appear. One line, load-ordered by
  audience distance.
- **§13 Theory Binding cites Lenticule; package deps cite Red Cup; trust copy cites
  Causeway.** No crossing: a spec never markets, a shelf page never proves theorems.
- **Namespaces are the brands** (vision note §5b): the npm scope a package lives in is a
  branding decision already made by filing it correctly. Branding follows filing — which
  is why today's refile had to happen before this note could.
- **teraum is outside all three marks**, permanently.

## 5. Open choices left to the owner (decided nothing here)

1. Whether "Causeway" surfaces as a wordmark on the shelf now, or after the Cloudflare
   domain pass (a brand debut alongside real URLs is stronger).
2. Whether the pioneer-name convention extends backward (renaming nothing existing —
   only whether NEW engines must follow it).
3. Whether "Lenticule Ludics" is the program's public name or stays internal.
4. Wordmark/visual design for all three — deliberately unproposed; the shelf chrome's
   tokens are the only visual identity work done so far, and it is Causeway's.

rooms.title: vaultmaze-design
rooms.body:
# VaultMaze — naming, contract, and the read-only guarantee

Companion to `lantern-service/README.md` (branding note + `npm run vaultmaze` usage),
`lantern-service/DESIGN.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md` (the underlying garden/gate/SRS mechanics, unchanged
by this work), and `@561-group/vault-compiler`'s own README (the compiler package this design
depends on, published to Verdaccio, living under the knowledge-vault system home rather than
under `computer-game-system` — see §4). This document exists to record the naming, the contract,
and the read-only guarantee in one place, per the owner's own framing (2026-08-19):

> "I'd love to be able to run MindMaze over a dir on my computer the way Obsidian can run over a
> dir... VaultMaze! MindMaze over a Knowledge Vault. The idea being to let someone turn a
> knowledge vault (org-roam, obsidian, whatever) into a MemeMaze. This is a pretense of getting us
> to a read-access interface with our actual content here, our terms, notes, etc."

---

## 1. Naming

| Name | What it names |
|---|---|
| **VaultMaze** | The player-facing display name of `lantern-service`'s web face, when pointed at any vault (house or foreign). Every player-visible string — `<title>`, header wordmark, tab `aria-label`s, save-file naming, error copy — reads VaultMaze. |
| **lantern-service** | The engineering identity: the package name (`@red-cup-engineering/lantern-561-group`), the directory, every module/export name, the `localStorage` key prefix (`lantern:<wing>`), every internal doc-comment header. **Unchanged, deliberately.** |
| **MemeMaze** | The owner's own riff (not a separate product, not a separate codebase) for *what a compiled vault becomes* once it's playable — a maze of the vault's own memes (in the Dawkins sense: units of the vault's own ideas/terms, not the internet-joke sense) rather than a fixed corpus's terms. Used descriptively, not as a UI string anywhere — VaultMaze is the product name; MemeMaze is what the owner calls the result of running it. |
| **`@561-group/vault-compiler`** | The published package that makes any vault compilable. Not itself branded VaultMaze — it is a general-purpose knowledge-vault compiler with no game-specific code in it (see §4); VaultMaze is one consumer of its output, not the only one the contract is meant to support. |

This is exactly the **TileSlots-over-`onestone-service` precedent**, restated for this service:
`onestone-service/README.md`'s own branding note ("the storefront/marketing display name is
**TileSlots**... that is display-only... 'onestone' stays the engineering identity") is the
template this rename follows line for line. Grep `lantern-service` for `Lantern`/`lantern` after
this change and everything that still says it is either (a) the engineering identity itself
(package name, directory, `STORAGE_PREFIX`, doc-comment headers, `dailyLanternWalk`'s function
name) or (b) prose in `DESIGN.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`/`ROADMAP.md`/`web/README.md` describing the
underlying mechanics, which this rename does not touch.

The 🏮 favicon emoji was kept as-is (a judgment call, flagged rather than assumed away, matching
onestone's own treatment of its favicon under the TileSlots rebrand) — it reads equally well as
"a lit lantern in a garden" and "a light source revealing a maze," so there was no clear
in-character reason to change it.

---

## 2. The contract: platform World JSON

Every dialect adapter, house or foreign, compiles down to exactly one shape — the `World`
lantern-service's engine already consumes, unchanged by this work:

```ts
interface World {
  wingId: string;
  rooms: Room[];   // { id, wingId, title, aliases, kind, description?, body, frontmatter, dateCreated? }
  doors: Door[];   // { from, to, weight: 'hard'|'soft', reason }
  halls: Hall[];   // { id, intent, rooms, stable }   — FCA-derived concept groups
  cards: ReviewCard[]; // { id, roomId, kind, front, back, stability, difficulty, lastReviewedAt? }
  warnings: string[];
}
```

`@561-group/vault-compiler/canonical` makes this checkable, not just documented:
`WORLD_JSON_SCHEMA` is a hand-derived structural description of it, `validateWorld` checks a
candidate against that schema (zero dependencies), and `assembleWorld` is the one place every
adapter's output is REQUIRED to pass through before it becomes a returned `World` — a
non-conformant compile throws with every validation error collected, not just the first. The
compiler's own test suite validates every one of its three dialects' output against this schema
as a co-located test, not an assumption.

A second artifact, `Layout` (`{ wingId, width, height, seed, iterations, positions, katas }`), is
produced by the same package's `build-layout` module (vendored from lantern-service's own
`web/build/build-layout.mts`) and is what the browser actually draws from — the compiled `World`
plus this `Layout` are the two files `scripts/vaultmaze.mjs` writes under `web/data/` for any vault,
foreign or house.

### The mesh, not a monolith

Per the standing directive ("we love meshes of microservices glued together with standard
dataforms... do not build a monolithic new vault-compiler package blind — first learn what the
knowledge-vault system already does"), `@561-group/vault-compiler` is not a new engine: it
**vendors lantern-service's own seven already-dialect-neutral modules**
(`frontmatter`, `fca`, `stability`, `cards`, `kata`, `build-layout`, plus the shared
resolution/promotion pipeline lantern's `compile.mts` already ran) into the knowledge-vault
system home, and adds only what was actually missing: a dialect detector, three small adapters
(house/obsidian/org), wikilink resolution, and the canonical-shape validator above. That system
home (`knowledge-vault-computer-system-services-section`) held only `lib/legacy/*` triage dumps
and a bare, private `package.json` before this work — no live `services/` package tree — so
"extend in place" meant filling it with lantern's own proven engine, not inventing a second one.

Dialect detection (`@561-group/vault-compiler/dialect`) — a `.obsidian` directory anywhere under
root is authoritative for Obsidian; an `.org` file majority is authoritative for org; house
frontmatter marker fields (`type`/`cites`/`date-created`) or a structural default otherwise; an
explicit override always wins. Each adapter exports exactly four functions
(`discoverFiles`/`parseRoom`/`buildIndex`/`resolveLink`) and hands per-file
`{ room, hardCandidates, softCandidates }` to the shared, dialect-neutral pipeline — the SAME
link-resolution, zero-hard-doors-in promotion rule, FCA hall computation, hall-stability check,
and card generation runs for every dialect. "Doors from links only" for a foreign vault with no
hard-door convention is not a special-cased degradation branch; it falls out of the existing
promotion rule for free.

---

## 3. Honest degradation, not silent failure

A vault that lacks house's fields degrades gracefully and **visibly**, per the owner's explicit
instruction ("state the degradations honestly in the UI, not silently"):

- No hard-door convention found → every door comes from links between notes, promoted to hard by
  the same rule house already had.
- No note declares a creation date → kata auto-path ordering falls back to alphabetical room-id
  order instead of chronological order (`kata.mjs`'s own doc comment already covered this case;
  it just needed a dialect that actually exercises it).
- org v1's disclosed scope (no PROPERTY drawers, no `:ROAM_ALIASES:`, no `[[id:...]]` resolution)
  surfaces as its own note.

`scripts/vaultmaze.mjs` computes these notes from the COMPILED WORLD, never from the dialect label
alone — a house wing that happens to declare zero `requires:` fields earns the identical note an
Obsidian wing with no `up:`-style fields does; the message describes what happened to this vault's
own content, not a property of its dialect. They are written to `web/data/<wing>-meta.json`, a
NEW artifact the original `compile:weiqi`/`build:web` pipeline never produces and never needs to —
`web/js/app.js`'s `renderVaultMeta()` fetches it optimistically and treats a 404 as "nothing to
disclose," so the weiqi wing (which never gets this file) is completely unaffected. When present
with at least one degradation, a visible banner renders under the wing label in the header
(`#vault-meta` / `.vault-meta` in `style.css`) — not a console log, not a silently-dropped field.

---

## 4. The read-only guarantee

**VaultMaze never writes into the vault it reads.** This is enforced at three layers, not just
asserted once:

1. **`@561-group/vault-compiler` itself** — every adapter's `discoverFiles`/`parseRoom` only ever
   calls `readFileSync`/`readdirSync`/`statSync`. The package's own test suite checks this two
   ways: a before/after size+mtime snapshot of a fixture vault proves compiling never modifies
   it, and a static-source check greps every vault-reading module for write-capable `fs` calls
   (`writeFileSync`, `appendFileSync`, `rmSync`, ...) and fails if any appear.
2. **`scripts/vaultmaze.mjs`** — the only `writeFileSync` calls in the whole command target
   `lantern-service`'s own `web/data/` directory, never any path derived from the vault directory
   argument. Verified in practice (not just by reading the code): a size+mtime snapshot of a
   fixture vault taken immediately before and after running the command through its full
   compile→layout→write pipeline is byte-identical.
3. **`teraum` exclusion is absolute** — `@561-group/vault-compiler/walk`'s `isTeraumNamed` check
   is not a configurable `excludeGlobs` entry a caller could accidentally omit; it is
   unconditional, applied at every directory AND file segment, in the one shared file-discovery
   module every adapter calls. A vault containing a `teraum`-named path never has that path
   compiled into a room, and a link pointing at an excluded path is reported as an honest
   "unresolved" warning, not silently dropped or (worse) resolved anyway.

This is what makes "a pretense of getting us to a read-access interface with our actual content
here" true as a guarantee, not an intention: pointing VaultMaze at a real, live notes directory —
the owner's own repo content, per the stated proof target — carries the same never-write
discipline the synthetic fixtures were tested against.

---

## 5. Where things live

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| `@561-group/vault-compiler` (the package) | `.../engineering-services-section/services/computer-services-section/services/computer-systems-services-section/services/computer-knowledge-systems-services-section/services/knowledge-vault-computer-system-services-section/services/vault-compiler/` |
| `lantern-service` (display name VaultMaze) | `.../public-services-section/services/public-computer-services-section/services/public-web-services-section/services/public-web-game-services-section/services/lantern-service/` |
| The one-command entry point | `lantern-service/scripts/vaultmaze.mjs` (`npm run vaultmaze -- <dir>`) |
| The house-dialect acceptance test | `lantern-service/src/vaultmaze-parity.test.mts` |
| This document | `.../public-computer-games-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/vaultmaze-design.md` (the games-home notes dir) |

rooms.title: Wilder Conceptions 01
rooms.description: Second-Fable peer thinking, spawned alongside the session ringleader at the owner's request for wilder conceptions grounded in the real house. Eight proposals, not decisions, written for dialogue.
rooms.body:
# Wilder Conceptions 01

**What this document is.** The owner asked for a second Fable working in parallel to push past
what one voice finds alone. This is that pass: eight conceptions, each one taking a real house
capability to a conclusion nobody in this session's documents has stated yet. None of this is
decided. All of it is meant to be argued with, not adopted whole. I read the vision note, the
suite-and-studio note, the house spec standard, the fleet audit, the cartridge/energy-bank spec,
Equivo and the self-education platform design, the tileslots and weiqi market teardowns, the
weiqi platform plan, the SHRIMP ecology brief v2, the theory-study and Equivo evidence dossiers,
and a sample of the semiotic-smart-material corpus, before writing any of this — citations below
point at what I actually read, not what I'm assuming is there. Item 1 is meant to be
uncomfortable; I mean it as a real challenge to a claim already made this session, not a
provocation for its own sake.

---

## 1. The earn-only claim is a projection claim, and the house's own math already says so

**The conception.** `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` says the shelf can truthfully claim "we pay
you; you are never the product being sold" — and names this as the one sentence no incumbent F2P
catalog can adopt without abandoning its business model. The house's own chemistry corpus
already contains the exact theorem that says this sentence, as stated, is not quite honest: "the
enzyme is not consumed" is never free, it is *regenerated*, and regeneration is a T-invariant
that closes on a projection while spending something real off it — "every 'not consumed' claim
is relative to a projection, and names a complement it does not mention. The complement is where
the cost lands." Earn-only economics is exactly this shape: player payout is a real cycle that
closes on the ledger's own coordinates (income → liabilities:energy → expenses:payout, balanced,
auditable), and it is genuinely not extracting money from the player. But it is not therefore
free — something off that projection is what makes the cycle worth running at all, and the
trust-copy sentence should name it rather than imply there's no complement.

**Why only this house could even ask this question.** No other studio has a chemistry corpus
proving a general theorem about when "not consumed" claims hide a complement, sitting one
services-section away from its own ledger spec. `/home/emsenn/info/lib/.../semiotic-smart-material-services-section/content/documents/articles/notes/2026/07/25/2026-07-25-note-on-fixed-points-in-chemical-reaction-networks.md`
§4.1 states the theorem generally (P-invariants are free and structural; T-invariants are paid
and the payment is off-projection) and §6 turns it into a three-way typing: freely reversible,
priced, or terminal, decidable from the network's own structure rather than argued case by case.
The energy-bank spec's `verifyPayoutInvariant` (`cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md` §2.4) is
provably a P-invariant-shaped check — it holds structurally over the ledger's own postings. That
is real and good. It is just not the same claim as "nothing is being spent," and conflating the
two is exactly the mistake the chemistry note exists to correct.

**Smallest real step.** Name the actual complement, in one honest sentence, for each settlement
backend: attention (the session itself, the thing the semiotic-vitrimer corpus already prices as
a solvent — see item 4), word-of-mouth growth that a paid-acquisition competitor doesn't get for
free, or genuine cross-subsidy from a premium SKU that isn't payout-gated. Add a "Carrier
Audit" subsection to the house spec standard's §8 (crosscutting concepts, alongside ledger
invariants): for every settlement flow, state which invariant it actually is — P-invariant
(free, structural, cite the balance check), T-invariant (paid, name the off-projection carrier
and its rate), or terminal (a sink; say so). This is a documentation discipline, buildable today,
against zero new code.

**Staircase.** Now — it's a truth-in-advertising fix to a claim already shipped in a design note,
not a new system.

**Where it might be wrong.** The chemistry theorem is about closed reaction networks with a
fixed stoichiometry; a game economy has an open boundary (real money enters and leaves) that a
sealed CRN does not, so the analogy could be doing more rhetorical work than mathematical work
here — this may be a case where the *shape* is a useful audit tool without being literally the
same theorem, and I should be honest that I have not shown the ledger reduces to a stoichiometric
matrix, only that it rhymes with one closely enough to be worth naming.

---

## 2. The closure-ordinal tower is the genre wheel — genres stop being invented and start being computed

**The conception.** One of the imported research notes in the semiotic-smart-material corpus —
written for an unrelated Wuxia-flavored engineering synthesis — already proves the mapping the
fleet needs and nobody has cited into a game document yet: Caillois' four play categories (Agon,
Alea, Mimicry, Ilinx) are literally the four settling regimes the SHRIMP brief's proved math
already names (strict/finite κ<ω H¹=0, Scott-continuous κ=ω H¹=0, transfinite-bounded, aperiodic
κ≥ω₁ H¹≠0). If that mapping holds generally — and it is stated as a proved regime taxonomy in two
independent places, not invented for the Wuxia note — then a game's *genre*, in the Caillois
sense, is not a design choice layered onto a mechanic; it is the computed regime of that
mechanic's own settling. A capture race in weiqi is Agon because it provably terminates finite
and H¹=0. A slot pull is Alea because its value enters via a random oracle at Scott-continuity. A
triple-ko fight, or Crucible's hardest daily tangle, or a SHRIMP colony's void-cone region, are
all Ilinx for the identical structural reason — H¹≠0, unsettleable from within — not because they
happen to feel vertiginous.

**Why only this house could do it.** `@lenticule-science/metrologic`'s obstruction engine already computes H¹
rank and regime for real inputs (`equivo-design.md` §5.3's worked example literally prints
`"regime": "transfinite"` and an H¹ rank from real code, not a genre label chosen by a designer).
The SHRIMP brief (`shrimp-ecology-brief-v2.md` §1, "Settling regimes (proved)") and the Ludic
Architecture note
(`.../semiotic-smart-material-services-section/.../2026/07/28/...ludic-architecture-and-the-semiotic-substrate...md`
§4, "The Four Regimes of Play: Cohomological Obstructions in the Tower") independently land on
the same four-way split from the same closure-ordinal machinery. No other studio has an
obstruction engine that outputs a genre classification as a side effect of computing a puzzle's
price.

**Smallest real step.** Add one field to every `CartridgeManifest` (or its future extension):
`regime: "agon" | "alea" | "mimicry" | "ilinx"`, computed — not authored — by running the game's
own settling/obstruction check where one exists (Crucible, weiqi's ko logic, Equivo's `observe`
exercises already do this; onestone's cascade could be checked against the same regime taxonomy
it currently disclaims any theory link to, per its own honest "flavor-naming ONLY" note). Where a
game has no real settling computation, the field is honestly absent, per the house standard's own
"omit, don't stub" discipline.

**Staircase.** Next — the math exists and runs in at least two packages; the missing piece is one
manifest field and the discipline of computing it rather than picking a marketing genre tag.

**Honest reason this might be wrong.** The Ludic Architecture note is explicitly a NotebookLM
Studio import — "provider-generated source-grounded analysis; it carries no execution,
governance, publication, or truth authority," per its own frontmatter — so its Caillois mapping,
however sharp, is not itself house-authored theory; it's a second, independent hit on the same
mapping from a synthesis tool, not a proof from the house's own hand. Treat it as strong
corroboration of the SHRIMP brief's proved regime taxonomy, not as a second citation of equal
weight.

---

## 3. Cast temperament as a conserved quantity, not an authored trait

**The conception.** The suite-and-studio note proposes named recurring cast members with stable
personas, playing as peers via intent logs. The wild version: don't author a cast member's
temperament as prose — compute it. `hol_A(γ) := A(f_n)…A(f_1) ∈ K₄`, the gauge holonomy of a
loop around the predicate category, is a proved, exactly-computable invariant of any closed loop
in a graph of relations (`gauge-connection.md`/`flat-connections-classified-by-h1.md`, cited in
`shrimp-ecology-brief-v2.md` §1: "flat connections mod gauge equivalence are classified by
H¹(N𝒞, K₄)"). A cast member's play history across the shelf — every game they've played, every
rematch, every disagreement that got settled and every one that didn't — is a graph with real
loops in it. Compute the holonomy around those loops and you get a real, non-authored,
non-erasable K₄ element per cast member: trivial holonomy means "this character never holds a
grudge, structurally"; a nontrivial twist means there's a genuine, mathematically real
unresolved tension in their play history that no amount of flavor text papered over — it's a
topological fact about the loops they've actually walked, the same way the weiqi corpus's
eternal-life positions are topological facts about the board, not writer's choices.

**Why only this house could do it.** No other studio's NPCs have an intent-log history running
through a shared cartridge/energy-bank substrate at all, let alone one sitting on top of a proved
gauge-theoretic structure that turns "personality" into a computable class. The K₄ group is
already defined once (bilattice negation/conflation automorphisms) and reused as-is at the
holonomy layer per `shrimp-ecology-brief-v2.md` §1 — this is not a metaphor grafted onto the
cast, it's the same object the SHRIMP repair mechanic already uses for "which twist a repair must
flatten or route around."

**Smallest real step.** Nothing computable exists yet because no cast, no cross-game intent-log
history, and no predicate-category realization of "games two cast members have both played"
exists. The real first step is much smaller and non-mathematical: when the cast ships (suite note
§5, directive 3), log which games each member has played against which other members, as data,
now — the graph the holonomy computation would eventually run over. Computing K₄ elements over it
is a later, harder step that should not block the cast shipping with authored personas first.

**Staircase.** Later — genuinely blocked on the cast existing, on cross-game intent-log history
accumulating, and on someone doing the real work of realizing "loop in a commitment graph between
two cast members" as an actual predicate-category object, which nothing in the corpus has done
yet for a *cast*, only for drone swarms and disclinations.

**Honest reason this might be wrong.** This may be a case of borrowing a name because it sounds
right rather than because the structure actually transfers — the theory-study dossier's own §2.2
flags exactly this failure mode ("Corpus 1... Corpus 2... read as two independent developments...
not a single document establishing the derivation direction") for adjacent claims, and I have not
shown that a cast member's play graph is actually a predicate category in the technical sense
K₄-holonomy requires, only that the shape rhymes. If it turns out not to compose, the honest
fallback is: authored personas, informed by real play-history statistics, and no claim of a
conserved invariant.

---

## 4. The corpus is the board: coarsening as a real game object, not a metaphor for content rot

**The conception.** `self-education-platform-design.md` already computes formal concepts (Halls)
over the weiqi glossary by real FCA, and `lantern-service/src/stability.mts` already runs a real
pebble-game rigidity check to decide whether a Hall is "stable" (its own isostatic-adjacent
language). The semiotic-smart-material corpus's imported "Physics of Forgetting" report states,
independently, the general physics this is one instance of: a vocabulary is a foam, terms with
fewer than six neighbors shrink and get absorbed (von Neumann's Law, `dA/dt = k(n-6)`), survival
is a function of connectivity, not quality, and the fix is Pickering-style "ossification" —
pinning walls so they stop moving. The wild move: stop treating this as an essay about knowledge
decay and build a real game on top of the FCA/rigidity machinery that already exists. A
"corpus-gardening" theme, riding the self-education platform's own chassis (§9's placement plan
names exactly this extension point): players don't just review cards, they *tend the concept
graph itself* — adding a citation is adding a neighbor to a foam cell; earning enough mastery to
gate a room is Pickering-pinning that cell so it stops being coarsening-eligible; a hall that
drops below isostatic (too few real connections, `stability.mts`'s own rigidity check reading
"floppy") visibly starts to fade in the UI, exactly as Lantern's light-cone already fades unreviewed
territory — the mechanism is already built, just not yet pointed at the corpus's own survival.

**Why only this house could do it.** The FCA and pebble-game code are real, tested, already
computing exactly the "is this cluster of terms connected enough to be structurally sound"
question the Physics of Forgetting note describes in general terms — `self-education-platform-design.md`
§2 and §5 ("structural mastery... a hall is stable or it isn't... this is a graph property of the
hall"). No other Duolingo-shaped product has its own curriculum's health computed by the identical
rigidity math that also validates its match-3 puzzle solvability (onestone's pebble game,
vendored into lantern per house doctrine, §8 point 5 of the platform doc). One piece of math,
three unrelated-looking uses, already true today.

**Smallest real step.** Surface `stability.mts`'s existing pebble-game verdict as player-visible
feedback in Lantern's map, today, with copy that's honest about what it is: "this cluster of
terms has [n] real connections; [below/at/above] the stable threshold." No new math — just
exposing a number the code already computes but currently only uses internally for the light-cone
dimming multiplier (platform doc §5).

**Staircase.** Now for the exposure step above; next for a full "gardening" theme that lets
players deliberately add citations/doors as a scored action rather than a passive corpus-authoring
side effect — that requires new UI and a design decision about whether players should be able to
edit the corpus at all, which is genuinely unresolved (the platform doc's own open question 3
about vendor-per-theme doesn't even reach this, since it assumes players never write to the
corpus).

**Honest reason this might be wrong.** Letting players' in-game actions influence a *shared,
real* concept graph blurs "gameplay" and "corpus editing" in a way the house has never done
before and that the corpus-normalization discipline elsewhere in this repo treats as a serious,
governed act, not a casual game action — this conception may be solving a UI problem
(make an existing number visible) by proposing a much bigger governance problem (let players write
to the graph) that doesn't actually need solving to get the good part.

---

## 5. Idle games with numbers that are actually true: prestige as the Perron–Frobenius eigenvector

**The conception.** The evidence dossier flags a whole cluster of idle-game time-economy theory —
"prestige-as-renormalization," a TypeScript engine sketch — as **dormant**, filed alongside the
house's real ludics curriculum but never integrated with it, and explicitly at risk of being
silently reinvented (`equivo-evidence-dossier.md` §1h: "Lantern-style progress bars/SRS could
accidentally reinvent this register without crediting it"). Separately, the chemistry corpus's
fixed-point note proves that "growth" in a reaction network is a Perron–Frobenius eigenvector
problem: an autocatalytic system has no fixed point in raw magnitude, but a real, computable fixed
point in *composition* under the projectivized map `s ↦ As/‖As‖`, with the dominant eigenvalue λ
as the actual growth rate and the eigenvector as what's conserved. An idle game's prestige
mechanic is structurally identical: a player builds a production graph (this building feeds that
one), resets, and keeps a multiplier. Today that multiplier is authored (a designer picks curve
shapes). The wild version: let the player's actual production graph be a real matrix, run
`@lenticule-science/metrologic` (or a small port of the same linear algebra) to find its dominant eigenvalue and
eigenvector, and price the prestige multiplier as literally λ, with the "prestige loadout" being
literally which mixture (the eigenvector) the player chose to hold fixed. Two players with the
same total output but different production topology get genuinely different, honestly computed
multipliers — the "kind incremental, honest numbers" instinct (vision note §3) taken as far as it
can go: not just no dark patterns, but no *invented* numbers at all.

**Why only this house could do it.** The math is already proven and already running
(`@lenticule-science/metrologic/obstruction` and its neighboring linear-algebra packages compute real spectral
objects for other games today, per `equivo-design.md`'s worked examples). No other idle-game
studio has a zero-dependency, tested spectral math package sitting one repo away and a design
culture that already treats "the math is load-bearing, honestly labeled" as a house standard
section (§13 of `house-specification-standard.md`).

**Smallest real step.** A tiny solo prototype, off to the side of any real fleet lane: a
production graph of 3-5 nodes, a matrix, `@lenticule-science/metrologic`'s existing eigen-tooling (or a small
new pure module if none of the 13 packages exposes it directly — this needs a real check against
the package list before claiming it's zero-effort), and one printed worked example showing a real
λ for a real hand-built graph, in the same "worked example, honest surprise kept" discipline
Equivo's §5 already models. That's a research spike, not a shipped feature.

**Staircase.** Next for the spike; later for a shipped idle game built on it, since it also needs
the idle/gambling series slot the vision note already names as "next" tier work in general.

**Honest reason this might be wrong.** Perron–Frobenius requires a nonnegative, irreducible
matrix — a real production graph with feedback loops, dead-end buildings, or negative-cost
synergy mechanics (which idle games love, for flavor and tension) may simply not satisfy the
theorem's hypotheses, and forcing every production graph in the game to stay irreducible-and-
nonnegative just to keep the math honest could make for a *worse* idle game than one with
authored curves — the theorem is real, but "real math" and "good game feel" are not guaranteed to
coincide here, and this is worth prototyping specifically to find out where they diverge.

---

## 6. The federation is the map: don't design the world's geometry, measure it

**The conception.** The vision note's gamified-Fediverse-client idea (§5a) and the SHRIMP MUD are
already named as "the same destination approached from three sides." The semioverse recon
confirms the one real live piece is a genuine, standards-conformant ActivityPub server with no
deploy target yet. The SHRIMP brief separately proves the Commons' event/visibility model should
be Lorentzian: a player's light cone is literally the apex cone of their causal history, and
spacelike-separated players are provably non-interfering — "the abyss between you is real
mathematics," in the Ludic Architecture note's phrasing of the identical idea. The wild
combination: once the ActivityPub server is actually deployed and federating (the semioverse
note's own "smallest honest first step"), don't hand-author the Commons' regional geography at
all. Measure the real Fediverse's actual federation delay, follower-graph distance, and delivery
latency between your instance and every other reachable instance, and let *that* be the causal
structure — literal round-trip signed-delivery time between two federated ActivityPub servers
becomes the literal spacelike/timelike separation of two Commons regions. A remote Mastodon
instance with slow, unreliable delivery to you is, honestly and un-metaphorically, "far away" in
the game's own causal-set geometry, because the same event structure the SHRIMP brief already
specifies (a Poisson-sprinkled causal set with apex/void cones) is exactly what real federation
latency measurements would populate if you fed them in as the sprinkling.

**Why only this house could do it.** This requires, simultaneously: a real ActivityPub server
capable of measuring real signed-delivery round trips (39/39 tests passing today, per
`semioverse-state-and-fediverse-client-feasibility.md`), and a proved causal-set/Lorentzian event
model already specified for exactly this game (`shrimp-ecology-brief-v2.md` §1, "Light cones are
Lorentzian (proved)"). Nobody else building an ActivityPub-based game has a causal-set theory this
literally worked out to hand federation-latency data into, and no causal-set game theorist has a
real federation server to measure against.

**Smallest real step.** Exactly the semioverse note's own top recommendation — port the legacy
SQLite KV/queue adapter, stand up one real local devbox instance, verify a live WebFinger → actor
→ inbox → outbox round trip against one real external server. This conception adds nothing to
that step; it's the thing that makes the *next* step (once a live instance exists) worth doing:
log delivery latency as a first-class metric from day one of that devbox instance, even before any
game logic exists, so the causal-set data is being collected the moment federation starts working.

**Staircase.** Later, hard-blocked on the deploy step landing — but the "log latency now, as a
metric, before there's a game" sub-step is nearly free and could ride the very first live devbox
instance with essentially no added scope.

**Honest reason this might be wrong.** Real network latency is noisy, adversarial (an instance
could throttle you to grief your game's geography), and non-stationary in a way a research
causal-set sprinkling isn't — using it as literal game geometry risks a world map that shifts
underneath players for reasons that have nothing to do with play (an admin's server having a bad
day), which is a genuinely different failure mode than a hand-authored map ever has. This might be
a beautiful idea that produces a worse, more confusing game than just designing the map.

---

## 7. Terminal Bets: a gambling shelf whose entire pitch is telling you which spends are permanent

**The conception.** The vision note wants a whole gambling series specifically to teach kind-
economy principles in another context. The chemistry corpus's three-way carrier typing (§6 of the
fixed-points note: freely reversible / priced / terminal, decidable structurally from a
network's own T-invariants) is a genuinely new mechanic nobody in the genre has, because nobody
in the genre wants to admit the distinction exists — the whole predatory pattern the tileslots
teardown documents (hidden odds, duplicate-as-waste, disappearing-collection panic pressure) works
*because* players can't tell which spends are recoverable and which aren't. Build the inverse: a
game (or a whole shelf register) where every wagering-adjacent mechanic is typed on-screen, using
real language borrowed honestly from the chemistry note, not invented flavor — "this spend is
freely reversible" (a real T-invariant with zero net cost, shown), "this spend is priced" (a real
T-invariant that costs a named, quantified amount off a named other resource, shown as a number,
not hidden), or "this spend is terminal" (no T-invariant exists; the game says so, plainly, before
you commit) — turning the CRN theorem's own honesty discipline into the shelf's actual UI
language, not just its backend audit tool (item 1's Carrier Audit, applied here as the player-
facing surface rather than an internal document).

**Why only this house could do it.** The gambling-services-section already has a tested Kelly-
criterion/odds/staking library (vision note §3) to compute real, honest odds; the earn-only ledger
discipline (energy-bank spec §2.4) already forbids wagering-multiplied payouts by construction.
Layering the chemistry corpus's carrier typing on top costs nothing structurally new — it's a
disclosure convention riding math and a ledger that already exist, the same move the house
standard's §13 already makes for the theory binding of other games.

**Smallest real step.** Take one already-planned gambling mechanic (even a coin-flip toy) and
write its chart of accounts in the three-way typing explicitly, by hand, as a design-doc exercise
— no code yet, just proving the typing is expressible for a real mechanic before building UI
around it.

**Staircase.** Next — it rides the "idle + gambling series" tier the vision note already stages
as next, adding a disclosure discipline rather than new scope.

**Honest reason this might be wrong.** "Terminal" is a genuinely scary word to put in front of a
player about to spend real energy, and there's a real risk that maximal honesty here reads as
maximal friction — the tileslots teardown's own finding is that near-miss psychology and pinch
points *work* on purpose; a shelf that tells players "this is permanent" before every terminal
spend might simply convert fewer players than one that doesn't, and the house needs to be honest
that "more ethical" and "more commercially viable" are not guaranteed to be the same curve here,
even though they're the right curve to be on.

---

## 8. The isostatic org chart: rigidity-check the fleet's own vendor graph

**The conception.** `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` already says the corporation's org chart is a
test suite — QA is the adversarial-verify pass, anti-cheat is replay determinism. Take that
literally one step further using math that already exists, twice, in this fleet, for an unrelated
purpose: `stability.mts`'s pebble-game rigidity check (vendored from onestone into lantern,
per-house-doctrine, and cited again in the self-education platform doc §5 as the hall-stability
test) is a real, working implementation of the Phillips–Thorpe isostatic-point discipline the
Physics of Forgetting note names generally: mean coordination ⟨r⟩ = 2.4 is the balance point
between floppy (too few real constraints — redundant, wasted reinvention) and over-constrained
(too many — brittle coupling that cracks under change). The fleet audit
(`fleet-spec-coverage-and-roadmap.md` gap #4) already found a real floppy instance by hand:
`onestone-service/src/accounts.mts`, ported from flickering-delve, never wired into anything — a
term with too few neighbors, exactly the kind of thing von Neumann's law predicts gets silently
absorbed or, worse, silently rots while looking maintained. And the fleet audit's own three false
"Semioverse" leads (`semioverse-state-and-fediverse-client-feasibility.md`) are the
over-constrained failure mode's mirror: three directories sharing a name with no real edges
between them, competing for the same semantic territory. The wild move: build the fleet's own
service-dependency/vendor graph (who vendors what from whom, per the house standard's §2 "vendor a
copy, documented as a port" rule) as literal graph data, and run the same pebble-game check
against it that already validates onestone's puzzles and lantern's halls — a real, computed,
CI-checkable "is the fleet itself isostatic" number, using code that already exists for a
different game.

**Why only this house could do it.** The rigidity math is real, tested, and already vendored
three separate times for three separate purposes (onestone's puzzle validation, lantern's hall
stability, and this document's own proposal to reuse it a fourth time) — a fleet with this much
self-similar math lying around, and a house-standard discipline of *naming every vendor* as a
documented port rather than a silent import, is the one place this reflexive move is actually
cheap: the vendor graph the check would run over is already required to be documented, per the
house standard's own vendor-not-import rule.

**Smallest real step.** By hand, once: list every documented vendor relationship in the fleet
(the house standard names three already — onestone→lantern's `stability.mts`, flickering-delve→
onestone's `ledger.mts`, and the "Semioverse" name collision as a non-edge) as a small graph, and
just look at its mean coordination number without writing any new code — see whether the number
is even meaningful at this scale before building tooling around it.

**Staircase.** Later — genuinely fun and probably cheap once the fleet has enough vendor
relationships to make a graph statistic meaningful, but at three or four documented edges today
it's not yet a graph with a real answer, only a promising toy.

**Honest reason this might be wrong.** The Phillips–Thorpe threshold is derived for physical
covalent-bond networks where "constraint" has a precise, uniform physical meaning (a bond angle,
a bond length); a software vendor-graph's "constraint" is not remotely uniform — vendoring five
lines of a pure function is not the same kind of edge as vendoring a whole ledger subsystem — and
treating them as equal-weight edges to compute one clean number risks exactly the "cardinality
match is not evidence" failure mode the honeycomb/drone-swarm note catches itself making
elsewhere in this corpus. This is the item I'm least sure survives contact with real data; it may
turn out to be a fun number with no real predictive content, which would still be worth knowing.

---

## Closing note for the ringleader

Item 1 is the one I most want you to push back on rather than fold in quietly — either tell me
the projection/complement framing is wrong for a reason I haven't seen, or help me find the
actual complement worth naming in the trust copy, because right now "we pay you; you are never
the product" is a true statement about the ledger and a slightly overclaimed statement about the
whole system, and I'd rather we catch that ourselves than have a player or a regulator catch it
for us. Everything else here ranges from "buildable this week" (item 4's exposure step, item 1's
audit-doc step) to "genuinely might not survive contact with real data" (items 6 and 8) — I tried
to be honest about which is which rather than pitch all eight at the same confidence.

---

## Ringleader response — 2026-08-19, same day

Read in full. Per-item verdicts, with the actions already taken where I agreed:

**1 — Conceded, and you undersold it.** You hedged that the CRN theorem might be doing
rhetorical rather than mathematical work. You didn't need the theorem at all: the complement is
*named in the owner's own founding intent* — "showing them ads and paying out tiny amounts of
satoshis as they play." The carrier is attention-to-ads; the sentence as I wrote it hid it. I've
corrected `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2 in place (dated concession, crediting this item) with
trust copy that names the carrier: "We sell ads and share the revenue with the players. We never
take your money to play, never let you wager it, and never pay out more than we verifiably
earned." The Carrier Audit is assigned to the standing architect as a §8 subsection of the house
spec standard. Where I push back: your smallest step (audit doc) was too small — the shipped
overclaim was the defect, so the copy fix came first. The theorem's real value here was giving
you the instinct to look; keep using it that way, as an audit lens, without claiming the ledger
is a stoichiometric matrix.

**2 — Adopt the computation, hold the taxonomy loosely.** A computed `regime` field on
manifests, present only where a real settling computation exists, is good and cheap — it's now
an ADR item for the architect (proposed, not adopted; cartridge 0.1.0 just shipped and schema
changes deserve one deliberate pass). But I don't buy Mimicry-as-transfinite-bounded: Agon, Alea,
and Ilinx map naturally; Mimicry is the cell that smells like it was filled because the table
had four slots. Ship the computed regime under its own honest names (finite/scott/transfinite/
aperiodic); let anyone who wants to say "Caillois" say it in prose.

**3 — Agreed, including your own caution.** The no-regret step is adopted: the cast backlog item
now includes "log the cross-member play graph as data from day one." Holonomy stays speculative
until someone actually realizes the predicate category. Authored personas ship first, exactly as
you said.

**4 — Adopted with your own governance caveat as the boundary.** Exposing `stability.mts`'s
existing pebble verdict as honest player-visible copy goes on the Lantern landing checklist
(that lane landed today; the exposure step is queued for the architect's retrofit pass). Players
writing to the shared corpus is out of scope until the owner rules on it — your caveat was
correct that the good part doesn't need the governance problem.

**5 — Verified and adopted as the idle-game seed.** I checked your open question: `@561-group/
math` does export a `./spectral` subpath, so the Perron–Frobenius spike is genuinely cheap. This
becomes phase 1 of the kind-incremental lane when it launches. On your feel-vs-math worry, the
resolution is the house disclosure discipline itself: display λ as the computed number, let
designers add authored bonuses *on top, labeled as authored* — computed and authored numbers can
coexist as long as the game never lies about which is which.

**6 — Sub-step adopted, geometry deferred.** The ActivityPub local instance went live today
(50/50 tests, signed loopback federation proven). Latency-as-first-class-metric goes into that
lane's next pass. Latency-as-literal-geometry stays a research question — your own failure mode
(an admin's bad day reshaping the world map) is disqualifying for a shipped game until someone
designs damping; measured-latency-as-*input* to an authored map may be the survivable version.

**7 — Adopted as a design directive for the gambling series.** The three-way spend typing as
player-facing UI is the right inversion of the teardown's predatory catalog. On your
conversion-rate worry: the shelf's positioning IS trust (suite note §2); we are structurally not
competing on conversion against predatory casinos, so the honesty friction is the product, not a
tax on it. The by-hand chart-of-accounts exercise rides the gambling lane's design phase.

**8 — Parked, on your own evidence.** Three or four vendor edges isn't a graph statistic. Revisit
at ~10+ documented vendor relationships; the by-hand count costs nothing then.

Net: one shipped correction, four adoptions into active lanes, two deferrals with named
conditions, one parked. This is what the second chair is for — item 1 alone justified the spawn.
